movies.title: 100 Days
movies.blurb: In 1984, the Brazilian explorer Amyr Klink sets out to become the first person to cross the South Atlantic in a rowboat. He charts a course from the coast of Namibia to Brazil and begins a hundred day voyage, facing sharks, storms, whales, and his own mind in the endless horizon. To find the strength to keep moving forward, Amyr turns to his past, searching the depths of memories until the adventure across an ocean becomes a quest for who he is.

movies.title: 111: Echoes from Halifax
movies.blurb: On 2 September 1998, Swissair Flight 111 crashed into the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Halifax, the disaster sending shockwaves far beyond the wreckage. Rather than depicting the tragedy itself, 111: Echoes from Halifax explores the lives forever altered in its wake.  Across continents, strangers become connected by an unimaginable loss: grieving families searching for answers, rescue workers and volunteers struggling to bring solace amid devastation, and the people of Halifax confronted with the enduring presence of a catastrophe  that arrived on their shores. As the search for truth continues and grief evolves, unexpected bonds form, lives transform, and new meaning emerges.

movies.title: 2.6 Seconds: Death in the Outback
movies.blurb: A gripping, cinematic documentary series that reconstructs one of Australia’s defining contemporary events, exposing the enduring legacies of race, justice, and colonial policing.

movies.title: 5 MORE MINUTES
movies.blurb: 5 MORE MINUTES tells the story of a couple at breaking point, who decide to spend a weekend away at an isolated house in the countryside. There, they meet the boss of the real estate agency, who shows them around the house and gives them the keys. But before he leaves them alone, the most extraordinary thing happens: the whole world enters into a time loop and the last five minutes are repeated over and over again, as if the needle were skipping on a record player.

movies.title: A Common Story
movies.blurb: Starring Alba Rohrwacher (Three Goodbyes, TIFF ’25) and Guido Caprino, writer-director Anna Foglietta’s heartfelt debut feature follows nascent empty nesters who encounter old desires while seeking new meaning in their lives.

movies.title: A Fireside Chat with Jordan Firstman
movies.blurb: As part of a new wave of boundary-pushing storytellers emerging from comedy, Jordan Firstman serves as writer, director, and star of his acclaimed feature debut Club Kid. This one-on-one conversation offers an unmatched look into the craft of multi-hypenate filmmaking and what it takes to shape a story from every side of the camera.

movies.title: A Girl Unknown
movies.blurb: In Zou Jing’s assured debut, Cao Ruofan and Li Gengxi (Bi Gan’s Resurrection) portray a girl passed through three different families and identities under China’s one-child policy. Visually refined, this affecting coming-of-age drama explores resilience and self-determination.

movies.title: A Good Little Soldier
movies.blurb: In Stéphane Brizé’s latest capitalist critique, Carla (Alba Rohrwacher) is pushed to her moral limits when she is recruited to rebrand a company’s image, compromising people for profit to serve her corporate supervisors.

movies.title: A Long Winter
movies.blurb: After his mother disappears during the first blizzard of the season, a young man refuses to give up hope as one long Colorado winter reshapes his relationship with his father and his understanding of the man he is becoming. From Andrew Haigh, the acclaimed director of All of Us Strangers.

movies.title: A New Creative Paradigm: Consistent, Cinematic AI Video Powered by Kling AI
movies.blurb: Presented by Kling AI, this panel explores how AI video is redefining the way cinematic stories are imagined, developed, and produced. Featuring an early look at Kling AI’s newest video model, the conversation brings together filmmakers and technology leaders to discuss how AI video can carry a creative vision from concept through production—with the quality, consistency, and control required for professional storytelling.

movies.title: A PLACE TO HEAL
movies.blurb: Lucia, 17, is brought by the police to the adolescent psychiatric ward in a public hospital, a place she knows all too well. Back inside, she reunites with her friend Eloïse, who is hospitalized long-term, and meets a new group of teenagers, each wrestling with their own struggles. Led by Etienne, the team of doctors treats, listens, and meets with families as they confront the raw realities of their patients’ lives, all while managing an overstretched department. Fragile bonds form between patients and caregivers, creating a delicate balance that offers glimpses of hope, recovery, and even laughter. But one day, the arrival of a mysterious new patient named Enzo threatens to turn everything upside down.

movies.title: A Rare Breed
movies.blurb: Hikers Mia and Erin stumble across a log cabin, miles off the grid and buried deep in the forest. There they discover Ray, a grizzled, dangerous veteran, who has taken a seemingly innocent young girl, Chloe, hostage. Mia and Erin can’t help but intervene – an ill-advised attempt to rescue Chloe soon sees them also captured, and they start to realize there are far bigger events at play. When the cabin is ferociously attacked by a shadowy group of mercenaries, the girls find themselves caught in a full-blown siege. And that’s when Chloe begins to reveal her true powers… From award winning short filmmaker Sam Johnson, A Rare Breed is a gripping, surprising, and propulsive sci-fi thriller.

movies.title: A Talent for Murder
movies.blurb: This smouldering chamber thriller from Anton Corbijn (Control) stars Oscar winner Helen Mirren and Alden Ehrenreich (Fair Play) as opponents in a strange confrontation between a youthful literary agent and The Talented Mr. Ripley author Patricia Highsmith.

movies.title: Adapting Real Stories Without Losing the Truth
movies.blurb: How do filmmakers transform real experiences into stories that connect with audiences while staying true to their origins? This conversation explores the creative and business challenges behind adapting real stories for film and television, from finding the emotional core of a narrative and making creative choices, to navigating development, financing, rights, production realities, and industry partnerships. Filmmakers, producers, and executives share insights into what it takes to move a story from inspiration to screen.

movies.title: After Elena
movies.blurb: When a family's matriarch dies, four relatives are forced to confront decades of silence, resentment, and buried affection. Led by Alfredo Castro, this sharp ensemble balances humour and melancholy in a moving portrait of grief and reconciliation.

movies.title: Ah Girl
movies.blurb: Winner of the Youth Jury Award at the 55th International Film Festival Rotterdam, Ang Geck Geck Priscilla’s feature debut is a bittersweet yet heartwarming story of a young girl as she tries to figure out what it means to become an adult.

movies.title: Alice
movies.blurb: Amidst the advent of modern cinema, trailblazing artist Alice Guy becomes the first female film director in this lush historical series starring Academy Award–nominee Bérénice Bejo (The Artist).

movies.title: All About Corinne
movies.blurb: Paris Follies writer-director Marc Fitoussi re-teams with the inimitable, Oscar-nominated Isabelle Huppert (TIFF ’16’s Elle) for this delectable comedy about a veteran background actor who spies a belated chance to break into the fickle family of le cinéma français.

movies.title: All of a Sudden
movies.blurb: Ryûsuke Hamaguchi brings Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto together in a poignant drama about friendship, illness, art, and the responsibilities of care, creating a film that makes the world seem gentler, more open, and more humane.

movies.title: All That She Wants
movies.blurb: Annie Murphy (Schitt’s Creek) stars in this effervescent, tender-hearted, refreshingly modern rom-com that chronicles a casual encounter between a millennial and a Gen Zer — and the life-altering consequences that result.

movies.title: Alpha Gang
movies.blurb: Léa Seydoux, Dave Bautista, Lily-Rose Depp, and Cate Blanchett star in the Zellner brothers’ look at an alien gang coming to Earth to conquer, but finding the human world has a plague they weren’t ready for.

movies.title: Alphas
movies.blurb: After a series of great white shark attacks threaten a quiet surfing beach, the sharks’ only natural enemy - killer whales - are enlisted to drive out the great whites. However, when the alpha of the great white sharks proves to be too powerful to stop, a former local surfing legend and a retired orca trainer come together to unleash the most dangerous killer whale.

movies.title: Always Lalisa
movies.blurb: K-pop idol–turned–global superstar Lisa stars in this intimate and transformative documentary tracing her journey from childhood ambition through BLACKPINK stardom into the artist she is today.

movies.title: American Hostage
movies.blurb: Jon Hamm stars in this adaptation of the hit podcast, which tells the true story of an Indianapolis radio reporter thrust into a high-stakes situation when a local man takes a bank employee hostage and demands to be interviewed live on air.

movies.title: Ancestors
movies.blurb: A haunting journey set in 1980s London, David Turpin’s mesmerizing debut transforms one young man’s search for a missing friend into an unforgettable story of love, loss, and gay legacy.

movies.title: Anchors Aweigh
movies.blurb: After a thwarted marriage proposal, alt-comedian Matt Barats spirals into an existential crisis in this semi-autobiographical blend of deadpan absurdism and unexpected poignancy told in a first-person, confessional style à la Ross McElwee or John Wilson.

movies.title: Angh
movies.blurb: In a deserted Nagaland village in the early 1960s, a chief must choose between his family and a transforming world embodied by an incoming American missionary in filmmaker Theja Rio’s gripping feature-length adaptation of his award-winning 2021 short.

movies.title: Apparition
movies.blurb: A Tokyo family prays for a miracle to save their struggling restaurant, and against all odds, it is the Virgin Mary who answers. But she arrives with an agenda of her own, asking the family to help spread her message in unfamiliar lands. As awe, confusion, prosperity, and hope ripple through the neighborhood, beliefs, rituals, and even the Virgin’s message itself are challenged.

movies.title: Arne Goes to Space
movies.blurb: An extraterrestrial visitor upends the lives of two elderly brothers in northern Sweden in Lars Vega’s disarming blend of sci-fi fable and small-town comedy.

movies.title: Arrested Memory
movies.blurb: A seasoned detective (Ethan Juan) recently diagnosed with dementia is doggedly pursued by both cops and crooks after he unwittingly wanders off with a multimillion-dollar ransom in a new absurdist crime caper from cult auteur SABU.

movies.title: Ashes
movies.blurb: Diego Luna crafts a powerful and deeply humane portrait of the immigrant experience through the eyes of a young woman forced to rebuild her life in a new country, delivering a nuanced exploration of family, identity, belonging, and displacement.

movies.title: At Night
movies.blurb: Mesmerizing and melancholic, the much-anticipated debut feature by British filmmaker and artist Beatrice Gibson is a work of choral autofiction that shifts from narrative to documentary to dream over a single night in Paris, reflecting on the nature of womanhood, privilege, and solidarity.

movies.title: Atonement
movies.blurb: Boyd Holbrook (The Bikeriders), Hiam Abbass (TIFF ’25’s Palestine 36), and Oscar winner Kenneth Branagh star in Oscar-nominated writer-director Reed Van Dyk’s searing story of trauma and forgiveness following a horrifying event during the Iraq War.

movies.title: Ba's Book
movies.blurb: In a hybrid documentary retelling, documentary filmmaker Ashley Duong takes her father’s memoir and stages a recreation of it in Vietnam alongside her family.

movies.title: Babies
movies.blurb: Seth Rogen and Oscar nominee Anna Kendrick (TIFF ’09’s Up in the Air) star in Lauren Miller Rogen’s big-hearted comedy about the dilemma that eventually infiltrates every long-term relationship: to parent or not to parent?

movies.title: BABY BANGKOK
movies.blurb: Set in Bangkok in 2059, William, a data obstetrician, implants the life memories of his deceased aborted daughter into an AI robot called "Bangkok Baby". Endowed with human emotional memories, the AI girl travels across the city in search of her mother. From an artificial intelligence perspective, the film interweaves oriental family affection with futuristic technology, exploring the boundaries between AI, life and maternal love. Blending soft sci-fi storytelling with human warmth, it depicts the struggles and bonds of innate human emotions amid rapid technological advancement.

movies.title: Back in Black
movies.blurb: Christopher Walken leads a terrific cast in director Ron Murphy’s hilarious satire about a failing family funeral home that experiences a reversal of fortune thanks to their town’s suspicious spike in fatality rates.

movies.title: Back to Buenos Aires
movies.blurb: Buenos Aires, 2008. After thirty-three years spent in Italy, Mariano Guerra returns to Argentina to testify at the trial against the former military officers who kidnapped, tortured, and enslaved him during the military dictatorship. Together with other survivors, he is hosted in accommodation provided by the Ministry of Justice, where he reunites with people who shared his captivity and waits for the day of his testimony. The days spent with the other witnesses, the encounters, and the testimonies bring back to light stories that had remained unresolved for decades. Mariano is one of the few survivors of that tragedy and carries a burden that no sentence can ever ease. His return to Buenos Aires forces him to confront what it means to have survived.

movies.title: Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo
movies.blurb: The latest from prolific maestro Takashi Miike, like Abel Ferrara’s Bad Lieutenant (TIFF ’92) and Werner Herzog’s Bad Lieutenant: Port of Call — New Orleans (TIFF ’09), is a sensational ride through the darkest crevasses of the criminal underworld.

movies.title: Bedford Park
movies.blurb: Writer-director Stephanie Ahn’s feature debut explores the complexities of diasporic experience through a chance encounter between two thirtysomething, second-generation Korean Americans, tracking their relationship as it moves from circumstantial to friendly to romantic.

movies.title: Being Heumann
movies.blurb: Featuring a breakout performance by Ruth Madeley and Oscar nominee Mark Ruffalo (TIFF ’15’s Spotlight), this inspiring historical drama from Oscar-winning filmmaker Siân Heder (CODA) celebrates the paradigm-shifting activist Judy Heumann, “Mother of the Disability Rights Movement.”

movies.title: BELIPHOOL
movies.blurb: BELIPHOOL directed by Aniba Rahman, follows a day in the life of Begum, the matriarch of a family of four generations of women. Set in early 2000s Dhaka, Bangladesh this film captures Begum navigating the everyday multitudes of joy and pain that come from building a home as a social outcast.

movies.title: Below
movies.blurb: Something monstrous lurks off the coast in this suspenseful, Newfoundland-set limited series, starring Josh Hartnett (Trap) and Mackenzie Davis (Station Eleven).

movies.title: Ben'Imana
movies.blurb: In this powerful, feminist debut feature, which won the Caméra d’Or at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo brilliantly explores the issue of forgiveness in the wake of the Tutsi genocide in Rwanda.

movies.title: Beyond Culture
movies.blurb:
Beyond Culture Launch at TIFF

Visionary Filmmakers, Jennifer DeLia and Mark Webber, are Co-Founders of Beyond Culture, a new artist-driven film and media studio, dedicated to transformational work that will push the medium and uphold a standard of excellence. B.C. honors powerful vision, supporting creativity that expands consciousness, celebrates shared humanity, and moves culture forward.
As part of the TIFF Speakers Summit, Beyond Culture will host an evening of conversation, community, and performance on September 15th 4-7pm at the Malaparte Rooftop in the TIFF Lightbox.

The evening will feature a curated panel of notable artists and visionaries exploring the future and power of storytelling, followed by a reception with food, bar and a special live performance by internationally-acclaimed artist, Marieme.

Speakers Include: Co-Founder/ Moderator, Jennifer DeLia; Filmmaker/ Co-Founder, Mark Webber; Actress/Producer Karen Strassman, Actress Eugenia Kuzmina, Singer/ Actress, Marieme, Actress/ Producer, Taylor Olandt; Artist/ Humanitarian Joel Bergner , Filmmaker/ Visual Artist, Matt Smiley, Actor, Brionne Davis & Actress, Taryn Manning

movies.title: Big World
movies.blurb: Liu Chunhe, a young man with cerebral palsy, overcomes physical and mental barriers while fulfilling his grandmother's dream and discovering his life's purpose, leading to transformation and a fresh start.

movies.title: Bitter Christmas
movies.blurb: With noirish hues and telenovela twists, the latest from Oscar-winning maestro Pedro Almodóvar (TIFF ’24’s The Room Next Door) follows a pair of self-centred film directors exploring grief, love, and the perils of unchecked artistic license.

movies.title: Black Sunflowers
movies.blurb: Black Sunflowers is a mosaic of Ukrainian youth, shuttling between the frontlines and civilian life, captured by the gifted American filmmaker James Marcus Haney (No Cameras Allowed) collaborating with an esteemed Ukrainian crew.

movies.title: Bleeding Hearts
movies.blurb: This real-life love story follows the charismatic musicians Zella Day and Jesse Woods as they team to create the alt-country band Chaparelle with collaborator Beau Bedford, in a documentary with as much drama as a season of Nashville.

movies.title: Blindspot Berlin
movies.blurb: This gripping thriller depicts the investigation — and its shortfalls — in the months before the December 2016 attack at the Christmas market at Breitscheidplatz, Berlin.

movies.title: Bollywoof
movies.blurb: A funny, heart-warming, and beautifully animated adventure for the whole family, Bollywoof follows Basil, a very British Springer Spaniel living his best life with his favourite human, 11-year-old Luke Price, in the Yorkshire countryside. But Basil’s idyllic world is turned upside down when the Price family relocates to Mumbai. After being accidentally loaded onto the wrong flight, Basil finds himself stranded in Kolkata—over 1,000 miles from Luke.  Lost and alone, Basil must navigate the chaos of a new country, narrowly escaping a relentless dog catcher. Along the way, he teams up with Santosh, a Bollywood-obsessed street dog, and Uma, a feisty holy cow. This unlikely trio set off on a thrilling journey across India, facing danger, discovery, and unexpected friendship as they race to reunite Basil with his family.  Bollywoof is a vibrant, action-packed tale celebrating friendship, connection, and the spirit of India.

movies.title: Brace Your Heart
movies.blurb: Amanda Kernell’s luminous third drama is a richly observed portrait of love, resilience, and the enduring strength of Sámi women in northernmost Europe.

movies.title: Bruton
movies.blurb: A tragic accident leads Bryan Bruton on a wild and unforgettable experience within the Florida prison system.

movies.title: Bucking Fastard
movies.blurb: Director Werner Herzog and real-life sisters Kate and Rooney Mara enliven the story of siblings who speak as one, fall in love with the same person, and eventually spiral.

movies.title: Building a Home for Independent Voices & Storytelling
movies.blurb:
In a landscape of big-budget franchises, algorithm-driven recommendations and endless content choices, where do bold, original and independent stories find their audience? As the premier streaming destination for independent film, Sundance Now sponsors this conversation with visionary filmmakers, curators and innovators to explore what it means to discover, share and celebrate independent cinema.

This panel will dive into what “independence” really means today — from production and distribution to curation and community — and how a streaming platform like Sundance Now can amplify independent voices and reconnect audiences with the spirit of discovery that made them fall in love with movies in the first place.

movies.title: Bunker
movies.blurb: Oscar winners Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem play a couple whose bond is tested when a mysterious billionaire’s proposal prompts an ethical impasse in the latest from Oscar-winning writer-director Florian Zeller (TIFF ’20’s The Father).

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: BURGUNDY
movies.blurb: The story of Burgundy’s most extraordinary characters and a celebration of the pleasure that defines their lives.

movies.title: Call Me Queen
movies.blurb: Anna, a British reporter, never expected to find kinship in Mercy, a sharp, fearless woman from Nairobi’s largest slum. But their bond grows, and so does their determination to act. As the AIDS pandemic devastates African communities and pharmaceutical greed denies access to treatment, the two women take on a fight far bigger than themselves.

movies.title: Carrie
movies.blurb: Vanguard of character-driven horror Mike Flanagan (Life of Chuck, TIFF ’24) returns to episodic storytelling with this kinetic adaptation of Stephen King’s classic novel, about the cruelty faced by a sheltered young girl entering high school.

movies.title: CASSOWARY
movies.blurb: On an isolated island, three generations of women live together, tied to one another, supporting and enduring each other. One summer, after a typhoon, their quiet life begins to shift in subtle ways. Su Min returns to the island, trying to pass through the cracks in life in search of the cassowary from the other side of the sea.

movies.title: Chernobyl-2: Life After
movies.blurb: Thirty years ago, a little girl watched her parents’ wedding, remembering the lilies in her mother’s hands. Today, she is getting married herself in Dnipro, a Ukrainian city living through years of war and air raid sirens.  Katya’s father was a liquidator of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster. He called himself and his friends “larks” — birds that are the first to rise into the spring sky — and called his struggle to survive after the catastrophe “Chernobyl-2.”  In 2022, a new catastrophe enters the lives of his wife Tanya and daughter Katya: Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.  Combining archival footage filmed more than twenty years ago with material shot during the current war, Chernobyl-2: Life After traces how one catastrophe echoes through another — and how a family living in the shadow of Chernobyl and war continues to love, laugh, endure, and move forward.

movies.title: Cheyenne
movies.blurb: Cheyenne follows a group of fearless cowgirls who compete at riding wild broncos on the rodeo circuit after nearly a century of being excluded because of their gender.

movies.title: Children Untold
movies.blurb: Acclaimed filmmaker and author Miwa Nishikawa adapts her forthcoming novel into a compassionate and clear-eyed postwar drama about a 12-year-old orphan who disguises herself as a boy, featuring a striking performance by newcomer Ami Koyae and a memorable supporting turn by Koji Yakusho.

movies.title: Clarissa
movies.blurb: Led by a stellar cast including Sophie Okonedo and David Oyelowo, filmmaking brothers Arie and Chuko Esiri’s second feature is a beguiling adaptation of Virginia Woolf’s Mrs. Dalloway set in contemporary Lagos.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Closing Night
movies.blurb: Naomi Watts, Sarah Paulson, and Odessa A’zion deliver powerhouse performances in Cody Fern’s sensational feature debut, where a hardened movie star reunites with the deliciously messy family she left behind decades earlier.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Closing the Gap: New Models for Financing and Distributing African Film
movies.blurb: The panel explores how commercially ambitious films from Africa and its diaspora can be financed, packaged, produced and distributed for global audiences. It examines emerging financing models, cross-border co-production, distribution partnerships and the role of institutional capital, with a focus on collaboration across the value chain to expand international reach and create sustainable value for filmmakers and investors.

movies.title: Club Kid
movies.blurb: In his exuberant debut feature, writer-director Jordan Firstman stars as a carousing New York City club promoter whose lifestyle is upended by the unexpected responsibility of raising a 10-year-old son he never knew he had.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Compound
movies.blurb: What happens when a family goes too far off the grid? Shot entirely on home security cameras - the same tech in millions of American homes - Compound documents the Williams family in the months leading up to the violent incident of June 10, 2025. Isolation breeds paranoia as the family fractures over their way of life, but when the outside world shows up to question their values, they are ready for battle.

movies.title: Congo Boy
movies.blurb: Drawing upon director Rafiki Fariala’s own experience as a displaced Congolese finding purpose in art, this rousing character study follows a young man trying to care for his family while forging his own path as a rapper in Bangui.

movies.title: Conversation With The Sea
movies.blurb: Condemned to pay the social security contributions owed by his son, a father (Kamel El Basha) desperately tries to prove his death in the moving drama Conversation With The Sea.

movies.title: Coward
movies.blurb: Belgian director Lukas Dhont’s poignant third feature celebrates a love that blooms amid the hardships and horrors of the First World War.

movies.title: Crystal Lake
movies.blurb: Set long before the events of Friday the 13th, Linda Cardellini stars as Pamela Voorhees in this captivating, A24-produced origin series.

movies.title: Daniel
movies.blurb: During the Jewish exile to Babylon, Daniel and his friends face trials as Babylon's armies conquer Jerusalem. Under King Nebuchadnezzar, they gain royal favor but make enemies. Their faith is tested at the fiery furnace.

movies.title: Darlene Love: I Know Where I've Been
movies.blurb: Stars like Bruce Springsteen, Cher, and Dionne Warwick sing the praises of an underappreciated musical icon in this high-spirited and warm-hearted portrait from Canadian director Barry Avrich (Oscar Peterson: Black + White, TIFF ’21).

movies.title: DAU
movies.blurb: Inspired by the physicists who built the Soviet atomic bomb, the film DAU follows a brilliant Greek-born physicist from 1928 through four tumultuous decades in the USSR. Driven to uncover the laws of the universe, the idealistic Dau is drawn into state service to help create one of history’s deadliest weapons. Inside a secret research institute, life is governed by scientific ambition, power, surveillance and privilege. As his autonomy erodes, Dau seeks freedom beyond his marriage through a succession of affairs, gradually losing both himself and his capacity to love. At once an intimate portrait of a man in pursuit of happiness and freedom and a vast fresco of a society founded on violence and ideology, DAU traces the small compromises that shape a life and alter the course of history.

movies.title: Dead to Rights
movies.blurb: During the 1937 Nanjing Massacre, a young postman named A Chang disguised himself as a photo lab technician to survive. He worked for Japanese military journalist Ito, developing photos, while secretly sheltering Chinese civilians and soldiers—including the photo studio owner Lao Jin and his family—turning the studio into a temporary refuge.

movies.title: DGC Visionaries @ TIFF: The Market
movies.blurb: Join us for a full day of fascinating conversations with some of the festival’s most thought-provoking filmmakers, diving into their creative process and unpacking how they do what they do—and why. Insightful, frank and funny, these sessions will reveal the behind-the-scenes stories of many of TIFF’s must-see films. DGC Visionaries is where the industry and the audience come together. One place. One time. Uniquely free and open to the public. No passes or tickets required. Hosted by the Directors Guild of Canada. Session 1 - 10:00-11:00am Helen Shaver, Below Moderator, Heather Hawthorn Doyle Session 2 - 11:30-12:30 Mila Aung-Thwin, The Ultra Runner Sean Menard, Run Terry Run Carol Nguyen, Still Night, Burning House Matthew Rankin, Ladies and Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney Moderator, Francine Zuckerman Session 3 - 1:00-2:00 Marie Clements, How We Stand Vinnie Karetak, In Alaska Alexandra Lazarowich, Turtle Island Rap Cody Lightning, Smudge the Blades Moderator, Danis Goulet Session 4 - 2:30-3:30 Mina Shum, Whatcha Want Gessica Geneus, Marie Madeleine Deepa Mehta, Moderator Session 5 - 4:00-5:00 Michael Dowse, The Stunt Driver Ron Murphy, Back in Black Alexandre Franchi, L’Autre Rodrigo Barriusso, Neverman Michael Kennedy, Moderator

movies.title: DIALOGUES Betting on Cinema: Warner Brothers’ Pam Abdy & Mike De Luca
movies.blurb: In an era of industry consolidation, shifting windows, and evolving audience habits, Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group Co-Chairs and Co-CEOs Pam Abdy and Mike De Luca have proven that backing bold, director-led cinema remains a winning strategy. Grounded in a 30-year partnership, the executive duo defied market cynicism by delivering a record-breaking $4 billion slate, balancing major franchise IP with high-stakes original hits like Sinners and One Battle After Another. In this candid conversation, the two pull back the curtain on modern studio leadership to discuss the mechanics of building a risk-tolerant slate, tailoring distribution for next-generation moviegoers and — as De Luca is quoted — putting the "tent" back in "tentpole."

movies.title: DIALOGUES Dissecting Genres and Trends of Southeast Asia
movies.blurb: With its growing global footprint, Southeast Asian cinema is the next industry to watch. Join the creative minds behind this year's standout Southeast Asian titles as they break down current trends, explore genre diversity, and share their outlook on what’s next for the region's roaring film industry.

movies.title: DIALOGUES Documentary Producers: How They Did It
movies.blurb: In these challenging times for documentary funding and distribution, producers are constantly finding new ways to pull off their projects. We hear from three veteran producers with new works having World Premieres in TIFF Docs: Dan Cogan (Rapinoe; Icarus); Sigrid Jonsson Dyekjær (Low Lies the Land; The Cave); Ina Fichman (Ba’s Book; Fire of Love). They’ll share experiences with multiple ways of getting films made, including international co-productions, pre-sales, and equity funding, as well as navigating agents, distributors, and Oscar campaigns. Moderated by Thom Powers.

movies.title: DIALOGUES Expanding the Blade Runner Universe: A Multiplatform Evolution
movies.blurb: The Blade Runner universe is expanding. As the legendary franchise transitions from the big screen to a highly anticipated television series, it is now entering the frontier of immersive entertainment. This case study breaks down the blueprint of adapting a massive intellectual property into a world-class immersive experience. Panellists will delve into the creative, technical, and business complexities of translating globally recognized IP into a compelling, interactive world that resonates with existing fans and captures new audiences.

movies.title: DIALOGUES Holding the Center: Producing Under Pressure
movies.blurb: Independent producers are the creative, financial, and emotional backbone of the screen industry, yet their own wellbeing is rarely addressed. Drawing on the findings of the EAVE Impact Think Tank 2026 Report, Producers in Focus: Mental Health, Resilience, and Support, this conversation explores the unseen pressures producers carry and shares practical strategies for care, resilience, and sustainable practice. Together, the panel will examine how producers and the wider screen sector can share responsibility for creating a healthier production culture.

movies.title: DIALOGUES Immersive Media is Revolutionary Media
movies.blurb: If film is a representation of the world, how does that representation change when the audience is at the centre of the story? Done right, truly immersive media gives the audience the agency to be an active participant in the storyworld. Tuned towards transformation, immersive media can be revolutionary media. This panel of rabble-rousers knows how to wield the creative affordances of immersive media like virtual and mixed reality. Come and learn the art and craft of immersive storytelling and how these experienced creators plan to use their medium of choice to change hearts and minds on some of the most important issues of the day.

movies.title: DIALOGUES Indigenous Actors Taking the Lead
movies.blurb: From global series to groundbreaking indie hits, a wave of Indigenous talent is reshaping the entertainment landscape. Bringing brilliant humour, fresh energy, and authentic storytelling to screens worldwide, these creators are redefining cinema. Join us for a panel featuring some of today’s most dynamic Indigenous performers, all recent alumni of TIFF’s creative development programs, to share their stories and celebrate the future of screen culture.

movies.title: DIALOGUES Local Sets, Global Laughs: Filming Comedies in Ontario with All That She Wants and Back In Black
movies.blurb: Discover what makes Ontario a premier home for world-class cinema. Join Scarlett Bermingham and Andrew Rhymer (All That She Wants) and Ron Murphy & Ella Ballentine (Back in Black) as they unpack their Official Selection films and celebrate the province’s growing presence on the global stage. From local sets to international screens, this conversation explores why filmmakers choose Ontario to craft their films, how Canadian film is evolving, and what's next for our home-grown industry.

movies.title: DIALOGUES On Adaptation: Hirokazu Kore-eda & Yeon Sang-ho
movies.blurb: Hirokazu Kore-eda and Yeon Sang-ho are two of East Asian cinema's most compelling storytellers. While their stylistic approaches seem to sit on opposite ends of the genre spectrum – from Kore-eda’s gentle, naturalistic humanism to Yeon’s explosive, high-concept genre allegories – their thematic interests sharply overlap. With their latest films premiering at the Festival, Kore-eda’s tender manga adaptation Look Back and Yeon’s chilling psychological thriller Paradise Lost adapted from a novel, these celebrated directors take the Summit stage for an unmissable conversation on the mechanics and the art of adaptation.

movies.title: DIALOGUES Producing in Times of Conflict
movies.blurb: Bringing together an exceptional panel of international filmmakers and producers, whose films are screening at TIFF, this conversation explores the realities of making cinema in regions shaped by political conflict. Drawing on their lived experiences, the filmmakers reflect on how they successfully navigate the ethical, practical, and artistic challenges of creating under extraordinary circumstances, from protecting cast and crew to overcoming censorship and production barriers. Together, they discuss what it takes to sustain creative freedom, adapt, and continue telling urgent stories through challenging times.

movies.title: DIALOGUES Serial Thrills: Writing Genre Series
movies.blurb: Audiences love the suspense of a mystery, the thrill of a scare—all things expected with genre storytelling. But how do you do that across many episodes? Join Kat Sandler, showrunner of Yaga and Brad Kane, showrunner of Crystal Lake, in a conversion on their highly anticipated official series selections. They will pull back the curtain on how to sustain high-stakes tension, build deeply immersive worlds and keep viewers hooked episode to episode.

movies.title: DIALOGUES Shorts to First Features
movies.blurb: Three of the Festival's most exciting emergent directors — including alumni directors of TIFF Short Cuts and Industry Talent — discuss their journeys thus far, from learning their craft and making short films to developing and directing their first features. Hear how Reed Van Dyk (Atonement), Carol Nguyen (Still Night, Burning House), and Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo (Ben’Imana) honed their projects, found the collaborators they needed, and coped with challenges, all while protecting their creative visions.

movies.title: DIALOGUES South-South Co-Productions: New Routes, New Alliances
movies.blurb: What happens when filmmakers stop looking North for their creative and production partners? Across Latin America and Africa, a new generation of bold, unexpected co-productions is challenging the traditional pathways that have long connected both regions primarily to Europe. This panel brings together the producers and creators behind Furies and The Smell of Apples, both premiering at the Festival, to explore the possibilities of building meaningful South-South collaborations: sharing talent, resources, audiences, and creative perspectives across continents. A conversation about breaking established models, forging new cinematic alliances, and imagining a truly global film ecosystem from the Global South outward.

movies.title: DIALOGUES The Internet's New Studio System
movies.blurb: As original series and short-form storytelling flourish across social platforms, a new studio system is taking shape online. This conversation, co-programmed by The Webby Awards, brings together creators, brands, and producers exploring new ways to develop, fund, and distribute entertainment. From brands financing original series to creators building worlds and audiences directly, the panel explores the opportunities emerging beyond traditional film and television, what it takes to tell great stories for the feed, and why some of the most exciting new storytelling is happening on the internet.

movies.title: DIALOGUES The OBSESSION Obsession with Curry Barker & Inde Navarrette
movies.blurb: Following its explosive premiere at TIFF’s Midnight Madness, Curry Barker’s indie horror Obsession proved that original, high-voltage genre cinema is alive and thriving. Powered by a visceral breakout performance from Inde Navarrette, the film showcased how two digital-native creators could leverage their online roots to reignite the theatrical moviegoing experience. Now, with major projects on the horizon, this conversation brings together two of the industry’s most exciting rising talents to reflect on their beginnings, unpack the transition from digital platforms to the silver screen, and discuss the collaborative craft behind modern genre storytelling.

movies.title: DIALOGUES The Stories We Tell: Advancing Accessibility Through Inclusive Storytelling
movies.blurb:
Accessibility is often misunderstood in entertainment, with most efforts focused on distributing content to audiences rather than shaping how stories are conceived and created. This conversation aims to shift focus away from technical standards and legal compliance, centring instead on the cultural and attitudinal changes required to make accessibility real.

This panel breaks down accessibility as a design philosophy that requires dismantling four barriers: physical, information/communication, systemic, and attitudinal. Joined by Official Selection talent and industry experts, this discussion will highlight how confronting attitudinal barriers requires inclusive storytelling, and how, without this shift, accessibility and disability inclusion efforts will fall short.

movies.title: Diane In The Loop
movies.blurb: Diane despises men as much as she desires them. Her mother was raped three years before giving birth to Diane. As Diane finds out, she has only one goal: avenging her mother. But Mom has one thing on her mind: finally becoming the woman she should have been. Between the one who wants to remember and the one who wants to forget, tensions run high.

movies.title: Diary of a Mad Old Man
movies.blurb: This captivating adaptation of Jun’ichirō Tanizaki’s novel from director Wayne Wang (TIFF ’93’s The Joy Luck Club) follows an aging widower drawn into an unnervingly intimate relationship with his caregiver daughter-in-law.

movies.title: Director Spotlight presented by TheWrap
movies.blurb: An exclusive one-on-one conversation with the director behind one of this year's featured films at TIFF. From the project's creative origins to the challenges of bringing it to the screen, the filmmaker will share insights into their artistic vision, collaboration with cast and crew, and the journey from script to premiere.

movies.title: Djinn Wedding
movies.blurb: Set in a remote Anatolian village, Ferit Karahan’s Djinn Wedding is an impressive family drama that unravels family secrets and conflicts across three periods of time.

movies.title: Dorothy
movies.blurb: Set in a world shaped by caste, violence, and toxic masculinity, two childhood friends grow up inseparable in rural Tamil Nadu. Their lives are transformed by the arrival of Dorothy, a woman whose compassion quietly challenges the world around them.

movies.title: Double Freedom
movies.blurb: Less follow-up or sequel to his breakout debut than a sly and clever echo, Lisandro Alonso’s graceful and extraordinarily beautiful Double Freedom returns us to the daily life of Misael, a solitary labourer in Argentina’s rural La Pampa.

movies.title: Drifter
movies.blurb: Fast & Furious alum Sung Kang directs and stars in this alternately melancholy and exhilarating character study of a lonesome racetrack custodian with a secret talent for drifting.

movies.title: Edward Said: Between Worlds
movies.blurb: Palestinian scholar Edward Said is profiled in his own words, drawing upon decades of archives, to explore the legacy of his groundbreaking works including Orientalism and The Question of Palestine.

movies.title: Eklipse
movies.blurb: As the highly anticipated 1999 solar eclipse comes and goes, everything that was shrouded in darkness suddenly comes to light in Eklipse, the feature-length debut of Austrian writer-director Manuel Wetscher, whose penchant for poetic realism brings emotional turbulence to a bucolic setting.

movies.title: Elephants in the Fog
movies.blurb: A village matriarch (Puspa Thing Lama) must choose between her heart’s desires and her duty to her community when a young woman disappears into the forest in this delicate, riveting thriller.

movies.title: Eleven Days
movies.blurb: ELEVEN DAYS is the true story of the longest prison hostage siege in American history—a gripping thriller about courage, sacrifice, and the ordinary people who chose humanity over fear. What does courage look like when survival is no longer possible? In the summer of 1974, as Watergate shakes America's faith in its institutions, the maximum-security Walls Unit in Huntsville, Texas is led by Jim Estelle, an idealistic corrections director who believes prisons exist not for vengeance but for redemption. Inside its walls, guards, teachers, librarians, and inmates live within an uneasy system built on trust—a fragile peace shattered when notorious Mexican outlaw Federico "Fred" Carrasco launches a meticulously planned escape that erupts into an eleven-day hostage crisis.  As Carrasco and his armed followers seize the prison library, a small group of civilian employees find themselves trapped between fanatical violence and the overwhelming force gathering outside. Among them are librarians Judy Standley and Von Beseda, whose compassion and unassuming strength become the moral heart of the siege. Refusing to abandon one another or surrender their humanity, they repeatedly place themselves in danger to protect others—even volunteering to serve as human shields in the desperate hope that innocent lives might be spared. Their extraordinary courage stands in stark contrast to the brutality consuming the prison, culminating in a heartbreaking act of sacrifice that forever defines the legacy of those eleven days.

movies.title: Elsinore
movies.blurb: Andrew Scott (TIFF ’25’s Blue Moon and Wake Up Dead Man) delivers his strongest performance honouring the real-life story of Ian Charleson, the Chariots of Fire actor who courageously pushed through AIDS to play Hamlet at London’s National Theatre.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Everest: The Other Side
movies.blurb: Professional ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson seek to ski down the North Face of Mount Everest, a feat never achieved, as the Oscar-winning filmmakers Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin (Free Solo, TIFF ’18) follow their journey, shooting for the IMAX screen.

movies.title: Everybody Wants to F*ck Me
movies.blurb: Taron Egerton gives a gleefully committed performance as a man determined to be viewed by potential paramours as the ideal catch in director Jonathan Schey’s darkly comic appraisal of modern dating and how some men signal virtues they don’t possess.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Everything Else is Noise
movies.blurb: Prolific Mexican-Canadian auteur Nicolás Pereda has delivered his sharpest and most amusing film yet with Everything Else is Noise, a sly, self-reflexive comedy of manners and mishaps involving a trio of women classical composers and musicians.

movies.title: Everytime
movies.blurb: A grieving mother and her late daughter’s boyfriend explore questions of guilt, grief, and forgiveness on a family holiday, in Sandra Wollner’s bold and haunting Un Certain Regard winner.

movies.title: Evil Genius
movies.blurb: Featuring David Harbour (Stranger Things) and Oscar winner Patricia Arquette (Boyhood), Courteney Cox’s second feature as director boldly dramatizes the chilling, darkly hilarious web of stories behind 2003’s infamous “pizza bomber” incident.

movies.title: Faith
movies.blurb: The spark of romance offers a hard-working single mother (Erin Doherty, The Crown) the chance to imagine a different future. But after tragedy strikes, she discovers that the man she may be falling for (James McAvoy) is hiding a truth she couldn’t have imagined.

movies.title: FAT
movies.blurb: When a routine doctor’s visit unleashes violent memories from childhood, Maeve is forced to confront the offense and the offender. To survive, Maeve must learn how to fight. Is the fight she needs revenge? FAT is a story of private heroism, detailing the blinding courage it takes to track down and face the monster living inside one’s body. Memories of Sexual violence from Maeve’s childhood ruptures her sense of self. She is pushed to the brink. Her flesh, literally and figuratively, becomes too much to bear. Maeve’s past is the tyrant of her present. She can succumb to this tyrant, or battle it into submission.

movies.title: Fjord
movies.blurb: Winner of the prestigious Palme d’Or at this year’s Cannes Film Festival, the latest from writer-director Cristian Mungiu is a gripping high-stakes courtroom drama driven by a profound moral dilemma.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Flies
movies.blurb: When a lonely woman rents a room to a father with a hospitalized relative, she forms an unexpected bond with his young son, in Fernando Eimbcke’s tender story about care, connection, and quiet transformation.

movies.title: FORTY LOVE
movies.blurb: At 21, Sacha Gallo only knows one world : tennis. Raised and relentlessly trained by his father, the two share a single goal – to win their first major trophy title in Paris. But the arrival of a charismatic new rival challenges everything Sacha thought he understood about competition, ambition, and himself. For the first time, he faces an opponent of an entirely different nature : love. A force as exhilarating as it is destabilizing - and far more dangerous than anything he has encountered on the court.

movies.title: Foster
movies.blurb: Haunted by his past and clawing his way through sobriety, Donald Foster (James Franco) just wants peace — one day at a time. But when June (Natalie Burn), a troubled addict, leaves her young son on his doorstep, Don is dragged back into the violent underworld he thought he left behind. Now hunted by his former boss, Brooks (Ron Perlman) — a ruthless crime lord who knows every secret Don swore to bury — Don must fight for redemption, protect the boy, and face the sins of the woman who pulled him back in… one bullet at a time.

movies.title: Four Seasons in Java
movies.blurb: Kamila Andini, the brilliant mind behind TIFF ’21 Platform Award winner Yuni, returns with another polished and picturesque film with a strong women's narrative, starring Indonesia’s biggest talents Putri Marino, Christine Hakim, and Arya Saloka.

movies.title: Freeing Flipper
movies.blurb: Executive produced by Academy Award winner Leonardo DiCaprio, Freeing Flipper is the extraordinary story of Ric O'Barry, once the world's highest-paid dolphin trainer, who has spent the last fifty years risking his life and liberty to set dolphins free. In the 1960s, Ric trained the dolphins behind Flipper, the television phenomenon that made America fall in love with dolphins on screen. Everything changed when his dolphin Kathie died in his arms in what he believed was an act of despair, transforming the industry's golden boy into its fiercest opponent. As founder of Dolphin Project, Ric has spent five decades exposing the hidden world of dolphin captivity, from marine parks to Japan's notorious dolphin hunts. Revered by some, reviled by others, he remains driven by one unshakeable belief: every captive dolphin deserves a way home. Built on rare family archives, dolphin-POV underwater cinematography, and covert footage, this is the story of a man who dedicated his life to freeing others—and now, at 85, must confront whether he can finally free himself.

movies.title: From Pitch to Production: IP Exchange, Children’s and Family Content
movies.blurb: TIFF: The Market sets the stage for specialized IP rights holders working with children’s and family content as they present their slates to decision makers and production companies to option into films or series. Through pitches that cross boundaries into the cinematic world, ten companies curated from across Canada showcase tried and true titles ready for the screen. Be in the room as sparks erupt on future adaptations and deals are struck in real-time.

movies.title: From Pitch to Production: IP Exchange, Drama
movies.blurb: TIFF: The Market sets the stage for specialized IP rights holders in the drama space as they present their slates to decision makers and production companies to option into films or series. Through pitches that cross boundaries into the cinematic world, ten companies curated from across Canada showcase tried and true titles ready for the screen. Be in the room as sparks erupt on future adaptations and deals are struck in real-time.

movies.title: From Pitch to Production: IP Exchange, Horror and Comedy
movies.blurb: TIFF: The Market sets the stage for specialised IP rightsholders in the comedy and horror space as they present their slates to decision makers and production companies to option into film or series. Through pitches that cross boundaries into the cinematic world, ten companies curated from across Canada showcase tried and true titles ready for the screen. Be in the room as sparks erupt on future adaptations and deals are struck in real-time.

movies.title: FROM SCENIC TO SCENE - How Thailand Shapes Global Cinema
movies.blurb:
Exploring how landscapes, local culture and incentives transform Thailand from a cinematic backdrop
into a global story engine.

What happens when location becomes part of the story? From the specificity of landscape and culture to
the people, knowledge and infrastructure that bring a production to life, this conversation explores
Thailand’s evolving role in global cinema and the ways in which place can influence story, production
and the creative process.

Featuring acclaimed Thai filmmaker Banjong Pisanthanakun and Cod Satrusayang, a Thai producer,
executive producer and consultant whose international credits include The White Lotus Season 3, The
Creator, The Gray Man and Extraction. Moderated by Raymond Phathanavirangoon, with opening
remarks by the Deputy Governor of the Tourism Authority of Thailand.

movies.title: From Script to Audiences: Building your Community
movies.blurb:
Most stories do not begin with a guaranteed audience. Some begin with people who see themselves in the story first. Whether rooted in a genre, a platform, a neighbourhood, or a culture, they help carry it farther than traditional discovery alone.
 
As converting attention into actual viewership becomes harder to achieve, communities are playing a growing role in what breaks through. Bringing together voices from Canadian distribution, social-first storytelling, online film culture, and emerging audience trends, this conversation explores how communities are identified, engaged, and mobilized across formats and platforms.
 
Panelists will discuss how to identify who your story is for, when audience thinking should begin, and what separates reaching an audience from building a community. In a crowded marketplace, what happens when your most invested viewers become your strongest advocates?

movies.title: Frontières at TIFF: The Market
movies.blurb: Frontières is the world’s leading international co-production market and networking platform focused on genre film financing and co-production.  Co-presented by the Fantasia International Film Festival and TIFF: The Market, this Frontières event is a showcase of genre projects presenting a majority of Canadian titles, aiming to facilitate connections between the project teams and industry members such as producers, financiers, sales agents, distributors and festival programmers.

movies.title: Furies
movies.blurb: Set in a bankrupt and sweaty Beirut, Rami Kodeih’s impressive thriller follows two sisters in need of money for an important surgery.

movies.title: Future Tense
movies.blurb: With Future Tense, Jenna Cato Bass deals with climate change, human guilt, and South Africa’s identity in this bold time-lapse story based in the near future.

movies.title: Gail
movies.blurb: This music documentary on an Our Lady Peace superfan follows her on the band’s 30th anniversary Canadian tour, and boasts an original score by Lesley Barber (Bonjour Tristesse, TIFF ’24), and orchestral arrangements by Eric Rosse (Tori Amos’ Little Earthquakes).

movies.title: GANJ The Treasures Of Shah Jo Risalo
movies.blurb: GANJ: The Treasures of Shah Jo Risalo explores the timeless wisdom of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai a Sufi poet, saint and philosopher. Through the lens of his poetic works referred to as the Shah Jo Risalo, the film retells the harrowing tales of Bhittai’s Seven Queens: Marvi, Moomal, Sohni, Leela, Noori, Sassi, and Sorath. Written nearly 350 years ago, these stories remarkably challenge patriarchal notions by portraying women as self determined, and devoted seekers of justice. Featuring analysis from renowned experts and poetry sung by the legendary Abida Parveen, GANJ seeks to globalise Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai’s legacy and firmly establish him as the first known feminist Sufi poet in the world. The title GANJ, meaning bountiful or plenty, aptly suggests that the wisdom found in Shah Jo Risalo are treasures waiting to be uncovered and the messages of courage, spirituality and love remain profoundly relevant today.

movies.title: Gentle Monster
movies.blurb: Featuring emotional performances from Léa Seydoux (TIFF ’25’s Silent Friend) and Jella Haase, writer-director Marie Kreutzer’s follow-up to TIFF ’22’s Corsage is a dual portrait of women trapped in moral maelstroms caused by men’s malfeasance.

movies.title: Girl Group
movies.blurb: Rebel Wilson writes, directs, and stars in this story of a pop star who, following a downward spiral, finds a new sense of purpose by assembling a bunch of young up-and-comers to form a group of their own.

movies.title: Glaxo
movies.blurb: Glaxo, Benjamín Naishtat’s riveting adaptation of Hernán Ronsino’s novel, transforms a single betrayal into an absorbing tale of guilt, loyalty, and memory, weaving personal tragedy with Argentina’s turbulent twentieth-century history through an atmosphere of mounting mystery and suspense.

movies.title: God Bless You, Mr Kopu
movies.blurb: A charismatic salesman promises wealth, success, and a fresh start — but at what cost? Alex Liu's wildly entertaining debut blends dark comedy, social satire, and a propulsive thriller into a sharp exploration of ambition and identity.

movies.title: Ground Floor
movies.blurb: On the eve of departure for the summer holiday with his wife Vera, Kristóf unexpectedly discovers black mold on the wall behind their closet. Overwhelmed with the situation and convinced it is caused by a water leak somewhere in the building, he begins knocking on his neighbours' doors in search of its origin. What seems like a simple maintenance issue soon spirals into a tragicomic housing revolution, forcing Kristóf to confront not only a crumbling apartment block but also the deeper cracks running through contemporary Hungarian society.

movies.title: Growth of the Soil
movies.blurb: Nobel Prize-winner Knut Hamsun’s novel about a farmer’s struggles in early 20th-century Norway gets a powerful and richly textured adaptation by director Hans Petter Moland and his superb cast.

movies.title: Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!
movies.blurb: Oscar nominee Rinko Kikuchi (TIFF ’06’s Babel) stars in this fantasy-fuelled fable from director Josef Kubota Wladyka (Catch the Fair One), which follows a Tokyo ballroom enthusiast as she dreams and dances her way through spells of bliss and sorrow.

movies.title: HALF
movies.blurb: Twin half-blooded vampires (Ranjith Sajeev and Aiswarya Raj) wage war with desert highway hijackers in a gory martial arts curry western from writer-director Samjad and choreographer Very Tri Yulisman (The Raid 2, The Night Comes for Us).

movies.title: Happily Ever After
movies.blurb: American Girl director Feng-I Fiona Roan’s sophomore film explores the definition of happiness through the lens of two sisters, backed by breakout performances from Xuan Chen and singer-turned-actress Shuhua Yeh of i-dle.

movies.title: Having a Moment: Canadian Documentaries
movies.blurb: Canadian documentaries are more plentiful at TIFF than ever before. We’ll hear from the directors behind three of those works making their World Premieres. In the Gala programme, Scot McFayden pays tribute to the legendary Rush drummer with Neil Peart: No One’s Disciple. In the TIFF Docs programme, Mila Aung-Thwin profiles a one-time bank robber who now tests the levels of human endurance in The Ultra Runner, and Alexandra Lazarowich follows three aspiring Indigenous hip-hop artists in Turtle Island Rap. Moderated by Real Screen editor Barry Walsh.

movies.title: Head to Head
movies.blurb: Iranian filmmaker Ghasideh Golmakani’s absurd and sharply satirical debut feature explores what happens when a female director forces male actors to wear skirts and headscarves.

movies.title: HOLY WOOD DUST
movies.blurb: Two-time Oscar-shortlisted director Victor Kossakovsky and superstar botanist Stefano Mancuso take us on an unprecedented journey into the life of trees. What happens to a stump the second after a tree is cut down? What does that tree think and feel at that very moment? "Holy Wood Dust" is an invitation to radically reimagine the plant kingdom from a new, groundbreaking perspective.

movies.title: Hombre al agua
movies.blurb: The latest directorial feature from Gael García Bernal (TIFF ’19’s Chicuarotes) is a psychologically astute comedy of manners for the modern age, following an ensemble of eclectic characters seeking to become something more than who they are.

movies.title: Hope
movies.blurb: In this madcap marvel from Na Hong-jin (The Chaser, The Wailing), a police chief (Hwang Jung-min) and deputy (Hoyeon) investigate a monstrous incursion upon their remote village, as a headstrong local (Zo In-sung) musters a hunting party to root out the threat.

movies.title: How Can I Help
movies.blurb: Eighty-year-old Mrs. Winkler’s world has narrowed to a single person—her daughter, Emi—after the untimely death of her beloved husband. Over the years, her grief has hardened into bitterness. When Emi accepts a theatre engagement that will prevent her from caring for her mother, a robot caregiver is assigned to take her place. Feeling abandoned and humiliated, Mrs. Winkler initially rejects the robot outright. Yet over time, an unexpected friendship begins to form. Can Mrs. Winkler finally confront her unresolved grief and find a way back to her daughter?

movies.title: How We Stand
movies.blurb: How We Stand combines magical realism, a story of sisters separated by tragedy, and a cast of rising Indigenous talent. Starring Amber Midthunder, Alyssa Wapanatâhk, Isabel DeRoy-Olson, and Cara Jade Myers.

movies.title: Hundan - An Echo of a Dirge
movies.blurb: Hundan – An Echo of a Dirge  In the rugged mountains of northern Pakistan, an elderly shepherd gathers his grandchildren beneath the open sky and recounts an ancient Burushaski folklore that has echoed through generations. As his story unfolds, two young hunters set out in pursuit of a majestic markhor, unaware that their choices will alter lives forever. Through the haunting voices of the mountains, the tale reveals a timeless struggle between human ambition and the fragile balance of nature.  Rooted in one of the world's oldest living oral traditions, Hundan – An Echo of a Dirge is the first feature film ever made in Burushaski, a UNESCO-recognised definitely endangered language. Blending breathtaking Himalayan landscapes with a deeply moving narrative, the film is a poignant meditation on memory, loss, and redemption. It celebrates Indigenous wisdom and reminds us that true survival depends not on conquering nature, but on living in harmony with it.

movies.title: I Am Mario
movies.blurb: A transgender taxi driver’s dream of fatherhood becomes a reality when he gets pregnant, forcing him to confront his own notions of masculinity while navigating unexpected social, moral, and emotional consequences.

movies.title: I Play Rocky
movies.blurb: Featuring a career-making performance from Anthony Ippolito, the latest from Oscar winner Peter Farrelly (TIFF ’18 People’s Choice Award winner Green Book) vividly recreates the story of how an unknown named Sylvester Stallone got Rocky produced — and became a superstar.

movies.blurb: When two childhood friends meet after years to fulfill the broken promise of climbing Mount Etna, Adele and Sofia realize that like the mountain, old wounds loom over everything.

movies.title: In Alaska
movies.blurb: When a suicidal Inuk teen accidentally pierces an oil pipeline with a bullet, the FBI launches a full-scale manhunt across the northern wilderness in this drama starring Noomi Rapace (The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo) and newcomer Leo Matthew Temela.

movies.title: In the Heart of the South
movies.blurb: In the Heart of the South is what Single White Female would be if it were set in Toronto, with an Inuk protagonist and a dash of supernatural elements, starring North of North’s Anna Lambe.

movies.title: In Waves
movies.blurb: Set under the confectionery pink and blue skies of California, this animated film narrates the love story between a young skater and a surfer who share a mutual passion for the ocean.

movies.title: Independent Film is Dead. Long Live Independent Film!
movies.blurb:
An incredible tool was developed in Toronto in the 1960's. Marshall McLuhan's lens into the nature of our relationship with media and technology was compared to Einstein's E = mc². Now more than ever that lens is needed.

Many of us were inspired by the idea of the "independent" part of the film business. Where original stories could be born and then find a path to a big audience. The purpose of the independence was to encourage the originality. 

 But what if the originality is getting zapped out of existence by the mediums in our hands and homes?

 The medium is the message, and the roar of the algorithm is drowning out the voices of our great storytellers.

Originality is to cinema as nutrients are to food. The most virulently addictive stuff tends to be low in both. Imagine taking the ingredients you lovingly grew in your garden and putting them on sensor-reheat in your microwave. All those good intentions don’t stand a chance in there.

What kind of new medium would carry a message more compatible with the delicious and nutritious kinds of stories we’re actually in short supply of? How can we move toward a future where these technologies enrich our stories rather than weaponize them?

Join this discussion with leading independent filmmakers and Andrew McLuhan. We will explore how to build true independence in today's industry, and unveil a new platform designed to empower the thousands of people whose labour makes the movies we love.

movies.title: INFINITELY DENSE
movies.blurb: Desperate to escape his loneliness, a man merges his mind with a limitless augmented reality system to shape existence on his own terms. The results are intoxicating. But as the system blurs the lines between his will and his subconscious, a psychological horror takes hold. He inadvertently unleashes dark, repressed demons, and his unhealed traumas become the true architects of his reality — proving the human subconscious is a force no technology can delete.

movies.title: Inherit
movies.blurb: Davika Hoorne plays her most magnetic role yet as Woranart – a grandma possessed by a demon – in the latest chilling psychological thriller by Shutter director Banjong Pisanthanakun.

movies.title: Ink
movies.blurb: Director Danny Boyle’s latest thrillingly charts the meteoric rise of Rupert Murdoch’s fledgling but instantly notorious The Sun newspaper as he and editor Larry Lamb create the blueprint for UK tabloid culture. Guy Pearce (The Brutalist, TIFF ’24) and Jack O’Connell star.

movies.title: Inside Telefilm: Funding, Partnerships and Audiences
movies.blurb:
Telefilm Canada plays a unique role in Canada's screen-based industry, from supporting feature films and administering international co-production treaties to advancing the reach of Canadian content at home and abroad.

Designed for producers at all stages of their careers, this intimate conversation will provide an inside look at how Telefilm works with filmmakers throughout the life of a project. Two of our National Directors will discuss how projects are assessed, how decisions are made, what happens after funding decisions are rendered, and how analysts and producers work together throughout the process.

The session will also explore what makes a project truly ready to apply, the importance of sound financing structures and audience strategies, and how success can be defined beyond a funding decision. Through the lens of Telefilm's Strategic Framework, the discussion will examine the many ways Telefilm contributes to a vibrant Canadian industry and supports Canadian stories in reaching audiences at home and around the world.

Whether you are developing your next feature, navigating a changing marketplace, or looking to better understand Telefilm's role within the industry, this session will offer valuable insight into the opportunities, priorities, and partnerships that shape Canada's audiovisual sector.

movies.title: Intermission
movies.blurb: Yonfan transforms excerpts from his 15 films into a brilliant, genre-defying meditation on cinema, memory, beauty, desire, and his own singular body of work, featuring Maggie Cheung, Chow Yun-fat, Sylvia Chang, Shu Qi, Daniel Wu, and many, many more.

movies.title: Iron Boy
movies.blurb: Winner of the Special Jury Prize at Cannes last spring, Pixar animator Louis Clichy’s gorgeous hand-painted animation tells the story of a boy in need of a back brace who seeks the courage to stand alone.

movies.title: It Will Happen Tonight
movies.blurb: Louis Garrel (TIFF ’25’s Couture) leads a charming ensemble in this decades-spanning divine dramady from Nanni Moretti (TIFF ’01’s The Son’s Room) that will restore your faith in destiny and the wild logic of the heart.

movies.title: It's My Time
movies.blurb: Led by Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh (Everything Everywhere All at Once), this inspired comedy about a woman on the road to magic-cube mastery is a story of galvanizing gamesmanship and ageless defiance.

movies.title: Jim Queen
movies.blurb: In the heart of Paris’s gay scene, Jim reigns supreme: the ultimate Gym Queen, influencer, and object of universal thirst. But when a bizarre virus called Heterosis starts turning gay men straight, his reign ends overnight. Unfollowed, abandoned, and stripped of status, Jim is left with just one  unlikely ally: Lucien, a devoted, scrawny twink with more loyalty than clout. Together, they plunge into the queer chaos of the Marais, chasing a rogue doctor rumored to have a cure.

movies.title: Josephine
movies.blurb: After witnessing an event, a young girl is haunted by the trauma of the disturbing incident, opening her eyes to the violence that surrounds her.

movies.title: Julián
movies.blurb: From the acclaimed studio behind Wolfwalkers and Song of the Sea comes a joyful adaptation of Jessica Love’s beloved children’s book about a young boy whose dream of becoming a mermaid transforms both his summer and his relationship with his grandmother.

movies.title: Ken Russell's The Devils
movies.blurb: North American Premiere of 4K restoration!

movies.title: Kick On
movies.blurb: Looking to prolong their night of partying, four youths are plunged into paranoid pandemonium after crossing a mobster’s volatile son in Nick Kozakis’ bloody ripper of a siege thriller.

movies.title: Kissed
movies.blurb: World Premiere of 4K restoration! Initially a controversial outlier, Lynne Stopkewich’s singular debut Kissed (TIFF ’96) is a subversive, tender drama about sexual awakening that shares the same ethereal atmosphere as erotic Canadian classics David Cronenberg’s Crash (1996) and Atom Egoyan’s Exotica (1994).

movies.title: Krux
movies.blurb: The feature debut of writer-director Tony Vahl delivers a powerful and stark portrait of moral collapse, societal panic, and the consequences of being on the wrong side of history.

movies.title: L'AUTRE
movies.blurb: Wild delusions and genuine dangers threaten a patient recovering from cancer surgery in this visceral and darkly comedic thriller by Quebec’s Alexandre Franchi.

movies.title: La Bola Negra
movies.blurb: Los Javis’ ambitious and captivating homage to Federico García Lorca sees the lives of three men intertwined in love and loss across eras. Featuring powerful performances by Guitarricadelafuente, Carlos González, and Miguel Bernardeau.

movies.title: La Gradiva
movies.blurb: A pack of rowdy French teenagers embark on a school field trip to Pompeii, where desire, passion, angst, and class tensions in the present unfold against the ruins of the ancient past.

movies.title: Labrador - Autopsy of Silence
movies.blurb: As a cargo ship sails through a storm off the coast of Basse-Côte-Nord, a cook is found murdered on board. From the perspective of Alupa Tulugak, an Inuit mechanic and friend of the victim, this story reconstructs the events as a thriller.

movies.title: Ladies and Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney
movies.blurb: This kaleidoscopic culture jam from visionary filmmaker Matthew Rankin (The Twentieth Century, Universal Language) details the rise of Canada’s 18th prime minister through a satirical collage of archival footage, television nostalgia, and national mythmaking.

movies.title: Le Faux Soir
movies.blurb: Inspired by a fact-based act of subversive irreverence in Nazi-occupied Brussels, Michaël R. Roskam’s thriller delivers a historical drama that feels more like a heist movie.

movies.title: LEFTOVER
movies.blurb: Jeevan leads a serene life with his wife Kaveri and their young son Sayanth in a small town in Southern India. When a revelation shakes the foundations of their family, that calm begins to crack, pulling them into the currents of caste, guilt, and consequence. Amid an ongoing tribal conflict and the echoes of uprisings in the forests, Jeevan is haunted by visions of his schoolmate. What begins as a personal reckoning expands into a confrontation with the fractures of belonging and displacement in a world that decides who gets to stay and who is LEFTOVER.

movies.title: Lemonade
movies.blurb: Lewis Brophy delivers a breakout performance in Kim Bartley’s compassionate debut drama about Irish teen, forced to leave foster care on his 18th birthday, who must find his way in a world that suddenly expects him to be a man.

movies.title: LES MISERABLES
movies.blurb: After enduring 19 years in prison for stealing a loaf of bread, Jean Valjean emerges a hardened man. He seeks redemption by reinventing himself as a respected dignitary under a new identity. He promises Fantine, a dying factory worker, to rescue and protect her daughter Cosette, who is being exploited and mistreated by the deceitful Thénardier family. As Valjean raises Cosette as his own, he is relentlessly pursued by Inspector Javert. Amidst the social unrest shaking France, the fates of Valjean, Cosette, her lover Marius, and Javert become intertwined in a turbulent, revolutionary Paris. Through struggles, sacrifices, and a deep yearning for justice, Valjean strives to complete his journey of redemption and offer Cosette a future of love and freedom.

movies.title: Life of Jorge Luis Borges
movies.blurb: With the erudition and insight of a literary scholar and the gumption of an amateur detective, Argentinian auteur (and raconteur) Mariano Llinás (La Flor, TIFF ’18) explores the life and fiction of the legendary writer Jorge Luis Borges through objects and places.

movies.title: Light Pillar
movies.blurb: A lonely caretaker, a dying film studio, and a seductive virtual world collide in Xu Zao’s formally daring animated debut feature: a melancholic, visionary parable about cinema, technology, alienation, and the fragile promise of renewal.

movies.title: Like Magic
movies.blurb: Blending archival footage, personal testimony, and a decades-long search for answers, Melissa Saavedra Gil transforms a childhood tragedy into a powerful exploration of memory, truth, and healing. An intimate and deeply resonant debut that illuminates both a personal story and a generation shaped by violence.

movies.title: London
movies.blurb: An experimental yet tender road movie about an enigmatic man’s shared commutes across Austria’s scenic West Autobahn — shot in-studio with vintage rear-projection techniques — Sebastian Brameshuber’s award-winning London is a rare work of technical prowess that never belies its emotional core.

movies.title: Long Long Night
movies.blurb: This deeply moving debut from Kyu Bock Youm is a radiantly detailed animation chronicling the peripatetic lives of a rhino and a penguin as they traverse a vast, ever-changing wilderness brimming with natural beauty and human-generated danger.

movies.title: Look Back
movies.blurb: Visionary auteur Hirokazu Kore-eda helms this tender and slow-burning adaptation of manga creator Tatsuki Fujimoto’s acclaimed story, following two young artists whose friendship and bond become the engine of their art.

movies.title: Love is the monster
movies.blurb: In a chilling dystopian thriller shaped by fear and inequality, Neto Villalobos Brenes follows a grandmother, powerfully portrayed by Paulina García, whose granddaughter's kidnapping forces her into impossible moral choices.

movies.title: Love of Your Life
movies.blurb: Featuring a beautifully understated performance from Margaret Qualley (TIFF ’24’s The Substance), this sweeping romantic character study from director Rachel Morrison (TIFF ’24’s The Fire Inside) is an exhilarating testament to loving fully, making amends, and moving on.

movies.title: Low Lies The Land
movies.blurb: Set in the breathtaking landscapes of Piemonte in Northern Italy, Low Lies the Land immerses us in the lives of three winemaking families facing an uncertain future.

movies.title: Magazine
movies.blurb: Set in New York’s cliquish literary scene, writer-director Alexandra Pechman’s feature debut chronicles the sentimental education of an aspiring poet (Lily McInerny, TIFF ’24’s Bonjour Tristesse) who becomes tangled in a web of eros, cultural gatekeeping, and office intrigue.

movies.title: Man in Motion: The Rick Hansen Story
movies.blurb: This galvanizing portrait celebrates Rick Hansen, the great Canadian athlete and activist. It chronicles his 26-month Man In Motion World Tour: a 40,000-kilometre wheelchair journey that raised millions to eliminate accessibility barriers and transform public perception of people with disabilities.

movies.title: Marie Madeleine
movies.blurb: Géssica Généus directs and stars in this vibrant reimagining of the biblical tale of Mary Magdalene, following a free-spirited Haitian sex worker whose serendipitous involvement with a repressed preacher’s son opens each to possibilities.

movies.title: Masc
movies.blurb: This debut feature from London-based artist Bertil Nilsson is a tender, unflinching portrait of self-performance, identity, and the quiet but persistent work of learning to exist as oneself in an often prescriptive world.

movies.title: Matter of Time
movies.blurb: Charlie Fleck, a 29-year-old aspiring videogame designer, is given the opportunity of a lifetime with a time-stopping device given to him by his friend, an eccentric Toy shop owner Gibbs.
