movies.title: Meet the Creators: the Innovation Hub, Session 2
movies.blurb: A show-and-tell from the creators behind this year’s Innovation Hub projects at TIFF: The Market, a selection of curated experiences that demonstrate the year’s best immersive storytelling. The panel will kick off with lightning presentations from each creator and end with a moderated panel discussion about the art and craft of immersive storytelling. Come and hear from the creators of The Clouds are Two Thousand Meters Up, The Big Picture, Reflections of Little Red Dot, and Tartupaluk.

movies.title: Memories of a Forest
movies.blurb: Katharina Rabl’s stunning debut feature toggles between loyalty and longing for independence, centring a doctoral student who must choose between carrying on her family’s legacy or forging her own path.

movies.title: MILO
movies.blurb: Alice arrives in a quiet provincial town and takes a job at a local café, blending easily into a life that isn’t hers. Her presence is no coincidence. She is there because of Milo, a young mechanic who works at a nearby garage. To him, Alice is a stranger. To her, he is someone tied to a past she has never truly left behind. As buried tensions begin to surface and Milo drifts toward uncertain ground, both are pushed to a crossroads: is it possible to rebuild a bond that shattered decades ago?

movies.title: Mimics
movies.blurb: Down-on-his-luck impressionist Sam Reinhold makes a pact with Fergus-a wicked, strings-attached puppet-that holds the promise to propel Sam to stardom, unleashing a nightmare that threatens the safety of those he holds dear.

movies.title: Minotaur
movies.blurb: After a nine-year hiatus, during which he fled his native Russia into exile, Andrey Zvyagintsev (The Return, TIFF ’03, Leviathan, TIFF ’14) returns with a reworking of Claude Chabrol's La femme infidèle, adapted to his homeland's current rhetoric of patriarchy and warmongering.

movies.title: Misty Green
movies.blurb: Featuring a career-making performance from Slow Horses’ Rosalind Eleazar and supporting turns from Daniel Kaluuya, Adam Driver, and Anna Kendrick, Chris Rock’s latest as writer-director brilliantly satirizes the bigotry and hustle at the heart of Hollywood.

movies.title: Mr. Nelson, Did You Kill People?
movies.blurb: Cult Japanese filmmaker Shinya Tsukamoto directs acclaimed Broadway actor Rodney Hicks and Oscar winner Geoffrey Rush in a harrowing, visceral, and morally urgent portrait of Vietnam veteran Allen Nelson.

movies.title: Muganga: The One Who Treats
movies.blurb: SOME BATTLES CAN CHANGE THE COURSE OF HISTORY.  Inspired by a true story Denis Mukwege, a Congolese doctor and future Nobel Peace Prize laureate, treats — at the risk of his life — thousands of women who are victims of sexual violence in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. His encounter with Guy Cadière, a Belgian surgeon, will breathe new life into his mission.

movies.title: Mushroom Cloud: A Hibakusha Story
movies.blurb: The documentary portrays the aftermath of atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Through the voices of Hibakusha—atomic bomb survivors—the film transforms history into memories of devastation, trauma, and survival. Hidankyo officers: Michiko Kodama, Terumi Tanaka, Jiro Hamasumi, and Toshiko Hamanaka reveal enduring physical and emotional scars, as well as discrimination. They describe the political and international obstacles that shaped efforts to support atomic bomb victims and abolish nuclear weapons. The narrative explores the pivotal 1954 Bikini Atoll Incident, which broke the silence and led to Hidankyo’s founding in 1956, with members attending UN conferences to advocate for peace.  Professor Peter Kuznick discusses how Eisenhower and many military leaders considered the bombings unnecessary, as Japan had already surrendered. He provides context on nuclear diplomacy, failure of the NPT and persistence of nine nuclear powers. Hidankyo officers persevere through adversity, culminating in the organization’s 2024 Nobel Peace Prize.

movies.title: Musk
movies.blurb: The Oscar-winning documentarian Alex Gibney delivers his most ambitious and epic work in exploring the history of the world’s richest man, Elon Musk.

movies.title: Muyi
movies.blurb: A teenager undertakes a fantastic journey in order to save her mountaintop village where men are forbidden, in Julien Chheng’s charming and magical animated feature.

movies.title: My Wife Cries
movies.blurb: With My Wife Cries — a startling, minimalist study in romantic misalignment — German auteur and Festival favourite Angela Schanelec employs her singular style to portray the crushing anguish and vertiginous confusion brought forth by marital crisis.

movies.title: Neil Peart: No One's Disciple
movies.blurb: Geddy Lee and Alex Lifeson team up with four revered drummers — Stewart Copeland, Danny Carey, Chad Smith, and Gavin Harrison — for an exhilarating and poignant tribute to late Rush legend Neil Peart.

movies.title: Neverman
movies.blurb: Broadway and cabaret icon Justin Vivian Bond stars as a transgender gay rights activist with worsening Alzheimer disease suffering from the treatment in her nursing home, in Rodrigo Barriuso’s poignant second feature.

movies.title: No Limbs No Limits
movies.blurb: When an Australian couple is handed a son born with no arms and no legs, they reject the world's verdict on his life — and raise a boy who will carry a message of hope to nearly a billion people.

movies.title: No Paradise if You are Killed by a Woman
movies.blurb: A Kurdish female sniper returns to Mosul to rescue her sister from ISIS, forcing her to confront the violence she survived and the shadows of the person she became.

movies.title: Nobody's Violence
movies.blurb: Larissa Corriveau delivers a striking performance as an enigmatic death-dealer in this bold, bracing, and Buñuelian feature by Denis Côté.

movies.title: North is Now: Indigenous Storytelling in the Arctic
movies.blurb: As the Arctic becomes increasingly important on the world stage, Indigenous storytellers are creating new opportunities for collaboration, co-production, and international partnerships. Bringing together leaders from across the circumpolar North, this discussion explores how Indigenous-led institutions are building sustainable screen industries, strengthening narrative sovereignty, and positioning Canada as a key partner in the future of Arctic film and television.

movies.title: Nosotros
movies.blurb: After leaving his Indigenous family for work in Guatemala City, a lonely security guard falls for a business owner at the mall he patrols, discovering an unexpected refuge and a new sense of self in a world not yet ready to make space for them.

movies.title: Obsession
movies.blurb: When a hopeless romantic makes a wish that his long-time crush falls in love with him, a sinister enchantment ensues in writer-director Curry Barker’s freaky and frightening feature debut.

movies.title: ODDITIES
movies.blurb: Two self-destructive best friends accidentally kill someone. After finding refuge in a roadside antique shop, an older woman initially offers help, but things soon take a dark turn.

movies.title: On Behalf of My Son
movies.blurb: Anchored by a deeply affecting performance from Rejane Faria, Gabriel Martins’ moving drama follows a grieving mother seeking forgiveness from the families of a tragic bus accident. What unfolds is a profound meditation on guilt and whether forgiveness is possible.

movies.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
movies.blurb: Conceived in 1972 by legendary filmmaker William Greaves and completed 50 years later by his son David, Once Upon a Time in Harlem is an essential work of living archive, documenting a lively gathering of luminaries from the Harlem Renaissance during a cocktail party at Duke Ellington’s home.

movies.title: One Minute to Midnight
movies.blurb: Léo, 49, just learned of the death of his biological father, whom he never knew. Before going to settle his father's estate in Italy, he decides to spend a few days in Paris where he looks back on his life.

movies.title: One Perfect Date
movies.blurb: After her overbearing father dies, Emma, a young woman with Down syndrome, seeks the romance and career she’s always dreamed of—much to the chagrin of her worrying older sister Blake. Blake was always the favourite child and now Emma must battle with her sister about everything from boyfriends to cupboard space. Although Emma tests the waters of social media and dating apps, what she really hopes for is to meet the young man she saw at her father’s funeral—she just needs to figure out who he is! And if she does find him, their meet-cute would technically be at her dead dad’s interment. Not the most Shakespearean of romances. She also wants to become “employee of the month” at the local grocery store, but to do that she must convince the manager to hire her. Trouble is, he's her sister’s boyfriend Brad, and he’s a real jerk. Brad doesn’t see eye to eye with Emma and he would find his life much easier if she wasn’t a part of it. Can Emma live her dreams, find love and a career, and do it before her sister shuts it all down? She’ll need the skills, smarts, and maybe one perfect date, to do it.

movies.title: Ontario Creates Happy Hour
movies.blurb: Open to all accredited delegates, the Ontario Creates Happy Hour is an open invitation to mix, mingle and build new connections with Market colleagues.

movies.title: Onwards and Sideways
movies.blurb: The latest from Oscar-nominated director John Madden (Shakespeare in Love) stars Oscar nominee Laura Linney (TIFF ’08’s The Savages) and Rhys Ifans (TIFF ’23’s Mother Couch) as strangers whose lives become entwined when both are diagnosed with Parkinson disease.

movies.title: Operation Cronos
movies.blurb: Based on real events, chronicles the relentless pursuit of the terrorists responsible for the horrific Barcelona attacks. With a high-stakes countdown, the film dives into the race against time from the perspective of elite state security forces, as they work tirelessly to capture those behind the tragic events in Las Ramblas on August 17, 2017.   On that day a terrorist drove a van into crowds on Barcelona’s iconic Las Ramblas, killing 13 people and injuring over 100 in a brutal and deliberate attack. Triggered by the Islamic State (ISIS), the assault was part of a series of coordinated terrorist incidents across Catalonia, including a second attack in Cambrils. In response, local police forces launched a swift and highly effective counter-terrorism operation - codenamed Operation Cronos - which became a turning point in the manhunt for those responsible. The bravery and rapid action of law enforcement were key to neutralizing the threat and preventing further tragedy.

movies.title: Our Loves
movies.blurb: The latest from Avi Nesher (TIFF '16's Past Life) is a gracefully woven drama about the ways that love intensifies and second chances are possible in the face of adversity and mayhem.

movies.title: Our Share of Sand
movies.blurb: After years apart, 12-year-old Maya returns to India with her mother to reunite with her father - a sandmining business man. Immersed in a world where labour, legacy and extraction collide, she forms a fragile bond with Kiran, a young worker.   After a tragic accident, a police investigation turns Maya into a key witness, with her father relying on her to absolve him. Torn between loyalty and a growing unease she cannot name, Maya begins searching for the truth. As her mother quietly unravels, Maya uncovers a pattern of silence, exploitation and repeated harm forcing her to confront her father’s deception and the family’s complicity she must choose to break.

movies.title: Oxygen Masks Will (Not) Drop Automatically
movies.blurb: The first-ever series from renowned Brazilian filmmaker Marcelo Gomes tells the true story of a group of young flight attendants who smuggle treatment drugs from America into the hands of patients with AIDS in 1980s Brazil.

movies.title: Painless
movies.blurb: Davide’s life is turned upside down by a tragic event for which he bears an unwitting responsibility. Devastated by guilt, he is driven to a series of seemingly irrational choices that gradually lead him toward profound consequences. Yet, through his deep emotional bond with Elsa, Davide may still find an unexpected path to peace.

movies.title: Paradise Lost
movies.blurb: A bus full of children mysteriously vanishes. When an altered version of a grieving mother’s son returns years later, she must grapple with the technologically revised reality she has created in this sharp thriller from Yeon Sang-ho.

movies.title: Pelechian Project
movies.blurb:
North American premiere of 4K restorations!

One of the year’s greatest cinematic gifts, this programme brings together five newly restored films by the pioneering Armenian filmmaker Artavazd Pelechian, each a harrowing ode to humanity, and its natural cycles of existence.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Academy Conversation: International Feature Film
movies.blurb: Now in its 70th year, the Oscar® for International Feature Film honours outstanding achievement in global cinema. For the first time, winners from select international film festivals, including the recipient of TIFF’s Platform Award, will be eligible for consideration in this category for the 99th Academy Awards®. This new eligibility criterion provides filmmakers with another avenue for their work to be recognized, championed, and celebrated. This panel brings together Academy leaders and global filmmakers to discuss the category’s legacy and impact.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Book-2-Film: Bookending the Business of Adaptation
movies.blurb: Pages transformed to the screen: books have been adapted to become some of the most celebrated screen-based works of all time. What makes a book ripe for adaptation, and how is the material’s originality and voice preserved? What strategies are employed to balance the demands of two differing industries, and how can the stakeholders work in tandem? Co-programmed with the expertise of the Frankfurter Buchmesse, this session hones in on the business of the book-to-screen pipeline through publishing and film professionals who shape properties from print to projection.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Congrats on the Film! When Can I See It?
movies.blurb: You made an independent film. Now you need to get it seen, and the old route is narrowing. Stephen Follows, one of the industry's most-cited data analysts, traces three-quarters of a million films from premiere to release and collects the experiences of filmmakers that took distribution into their own hands. This session turns it into a practical playbook for filmmakers who control their rights: what it really costs, how long it really takes, what actually works, and the lessons from a hundred films that did it themselves.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Demystifying Film Financing
movies.blurb: Art is unpredictable. The financing doesn’t have to be. You’ve got the script. You’ve got the budget. Now it’s time to raise the funds. Where are those elusive wealthy investors and financiers and how do you navigate equity, debt financing, and what exactly is a waterfall? This crucial conversation will dive into risk engineering in the creative industries: slate diversification, completion bonds, multiple revenue streams, and more. This peek behind the financier’s curtain will set you on the right path because you may not be able to eliminate your creative risk, but you can learn to structure your financial risk.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Documentary State of the Industry
movies.blurb: We hear no end of pessimistic forecasts about the documentary industry. And yet films are still getting made and breaking through to audiences. We’ll hear from three figures with deep experience in the North American marketplace: CAA sales agent Amanda Lebow, who’s representing two World Premieres in TIFF Docs: Cheyenne and Bleeding Hearts; Kino Lorber president Richard Lorber, whose recent theatrical docs include the Oscar-winning Mr Nobody Against Putin and the summer arthouse hit Mary Oliver: Saved by the Beauty of the World; and Michael Tuckman, who’s had great recent success with the theatrical booking of the Oscar-winning No Other Land and the sleeper hit Secret Mall Apartment.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Equity and Parity in Independent Film: The Ethos Model with Clint Bentley, Greg Kwedar, and Colman Domingo
movies.blurb: Join Clint Bentley, Greg Kwedar, and moderator Colman Domingo for a discussion on the challenges facing independent film and how a parity model pioneered by Bentley and Kwedar on their films Jockey (TIFF ’21) and Sing Sing (TIFF ’23) made these films possible and gave them a chance to succeed for every artist, creative, and stakeholder.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Everything Old is IP Again
movies.blurb: Canadian stories are as vast and diverse as our country’s terrain. Our rich histories provide a landscape for creative, authentic, and above all, entertaining storytelling that has inevitably built an incredible library of IP. Canadian creators are finding new ways to renovate, reinvigorate, and expand on beloved characters — real and imagined. Join this impressive group of Canadian creators as we delve into the business, the creativity, and the maintenance and ownership of IP.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Expanding IP: The Opportunity and the Risk
movies.blurb: Gaming, film, and beyond: expanding IP across media can breathe new life into worlds and characters. But why do some IPs grow stronger with every extension, while others gradually lose what made them valuable? Drawing on more than a decade of helping game studios and publishers build lasting franchises, Christian Fonnesbech, CEO and Head of IP at Leverage Partnership, will define how to protect an IP’s emotional core and artistry, and how early creative decisions and later extension choices can shape its long-term value. What must be preserved? What can change? What do existing fans expect? And what must different creative industries understand before working together?

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Financing in the Age of AI
movies.blurb: As artificial intelligence increasingly transforms project development and production, this panel brings together major screen funders to discuss how the use of AI affects your funding applications. Hear from our guests about evolving evaluation criteria and policies that aim to balance technological innovation and human-driven, authentic storytelling.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Focus on French-Language Series Co-productions
movies.blurb: Join leading French-speaking producers and broadcasters from Quebec, Canada, and France as they discuss the creative and financial strategies behind successful French-language series co-productions. Discover how creators, producers, and broadcasters from French-speaking markets collaborate to create acclaimed series such as Empathie and TIFF ’26 Primetime Official Selection Alice. This panel will be conducted in French, with live English translation.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Fright Night to Spotlight: Making It in Cinema
movies.blurb: Horror is cinema’s single most effective career launcher, giving new filmmakers the rare power to transform micro-budgets into major buzz and turning unknown filmmakers into the next big thing. In this candid session, working producers and directors break down why fear is cinema’s most lucrative launchpad, share the creative and commercial playbooks they used to finance their features, and discuss how to turn low-budget scares into lasting careers.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES From the Front Lines: Producer Advocates on the State of the Screen Economy
movies.blurb: To understand where the screen industry stands today, we look to the international producing bodies on the front lines of trade policy, copyright legislation, labour agreements, and regulatory frameworks. Featuring leadership from CMPA, PGA, and EPC, this session explores how critical policy battles are reshaping independent production, proving why these advocates are the ultimate barometer for the global media economy.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Funding Without Borders: Unlocking Regional and Global Funds
movies.blurb: Regional grants and international film funds serve as crucial financial backbones for independent world cinema. Join us for a session with key fund representatives to demystify available grants, labs, and co-production schemes. Attendees will gain actionable advice on aligning their projects with fund criteria, navigating co-production requirements, and integrating international soft money into their film's financing plan.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Global TV Series Buyers and Commissioners in Focus
movies.blurb: As the scripted television landscape continues to become increasingly competitive, understanding what TV buyers and commissioners are looking for is critical. This panel brings together leading global commissioners, acquisition executives, and content buyers from different markets to discuss the current commissioning landscape, what drives audiences today, and the genres and formats gaining traction. Panelists will also share what drives their editorial and programming strategies. Gain insight into the key factors they consider when evaluating which projects to finance, acquire, and bring to audiences and learn how creators and producers can better position their projects for success.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES How Documentaries Find Their Audience
movies.blurb: With the success of streaming, true-crime, and constant content, more documentaries are being made than ever before, but with public broadcasters pulling back and theatrical windows closing, the infrastructure that once carried these films to their audience hasn’t been rebuilt to reflect the new landscape.  Join us for a conversation between a documentarian, a curator whose Instagram feed reaches more documentary lovers than several major broadcasters combined, and a researcher mapping the gap between them as they sit down to ask: how do films find their audiences now, and who's left doing the work of pointing people toward the stories that matter?

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES How Nollywood is Capturing Global Screens
movies.blurb: Join us for a high-impact panel discussion exploring Nollywood’s transformation from a regional powerhouse into a dominant force on the global screen. Leading producers, Moses Babatope & Mo Abudu, will unpack how streaming deals, box office strategies, financing models and authentic storytelling are going global while transforming Africa’s creative economy.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES In Short: What Short Film Programmers Want
movies.blurb: Explore the power of short film programming as an act of artistic advocacy. A panel of festival programmers from Clermont-Ferrand, FNC and Palm Springs join moderator and TIFF Short Cuts programmer Sonja Baksa to discuss how they construct distinct curatorial voices, champion experimental and non-linear forms, and defend short cinema as a vital, uncompromising medium in its own right.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Location Strategy Without Compromise: Accessibility and Authenticity in Being Heumann
movies.blurb: The set of Being Heumann balanced a historically accurate 1970s time period with actors who required environments offering mobility access and accommodations. How did the crew, film commissioners, and local advisors collaborate to ensure there was both authenticity and inclusivity throughout the sets on the Toronto-based locations?

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES New Partnerships, New Possibilities in Series Financing
movies.blurb: After years of rapid expansion, the series broadcast and streaming landscape has entered a new phase. What are the emerging financing models? Are alliances between traditional decision-makers, streamers, and international partners the key to moving forward? And how are producers adapting their creative choices to stand out in today's crowded market? This conversation brings together industry leaders to explore these questions and unpack how series are developed and financed today.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Producers with Killer Instincts
movies.blurb: As the creative force behind Killer Films, legendary producers Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler are the blueprint for how bold independent cinema survives. From helping shape New Queer Cinema to shepherding classics like Boys Don’t Cry, Carol, and Past Lives, they have spent thirty years turning risky, uncompromising stories into award-winning cultural touchstones. Hear how they defy industry odds, champion visionary directors, and navigate today’s shifting film landscape.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES Taking IP Live: Successful Touring Exhibitions
movies.blurb: As audiences increasingly seek experiences they can step inside, creative studios are finding new ways to bring established IP into the live space. This panel brings together the studios behind some of the most successful touring exhibitions to explore how beloved film, television, gaming, and entertainment properties are translated into compelling real-world experiences. From immersive storytelling and interactive design to audience engagement and global scalability, the conversation will examine the creative and business strategies that allow live experiences to extend the reach, relevance, and impact of iconic brands beyond the screen.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES The Global Rise of Microdramas: New Stories Captivating the World
movies.blurb: Microdramas are rapidly reshaping the entertainment landscape, proving that compelling stories can be told in just minutes. As the format attracts millions of viewers across mobile platforms and enters the cultural zeitgeist, how are creators embracing this new form of storytelling? This panel brings together international creators and producers to discuss how they are innovating within the format, engaging audiences, and redefining short-form entertainment.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES The Global Sales Playbook
movies.blurb: Join sales heavyweights Roeg Sutherland (CAA) and Glen Basner (FilmNation Entertainment) for a spirited discussion about evolving cinema networks, how leaders package and represent films, and how the screen sector is building global bridges to support creators and connect audiences worldwide. Designed for filmmakers, sales agents, and producers eager to maximize their impact, this session reveals what it takes to leverage your content for international sales, navigate distribution, and connect with audiences both overseas and in your own backyard.

movies.title: PERSPECTIVES The Role Hollywood Didn't Know it Needed: The Immersive Supervisor
movies.blurb: Audiences aren't just watching films and TV anymore. They're scattering across VR headsets, AR glasses, and platforms that didn't exist a few years ago — the IP is the same, but the formats keep multiplying, yet most productions still treat anything beyond the flat screen as an afterthought. This panel puts a name to the creative voice that changes that: a new kind of role called the Immersive Supervisor, in the room and on set, whose job from the very start is to help traditional filmmakers navigate emerging mediums. Drawing on award-winning immersive productions, a producer, an executive, and a practitioner explore why immersive thinking belongs in prep, not post, and how today's productions can unlock new value from their IP and stay ahead as the industry enters its next platform shift.

movies.title: Phoolan
movies.blurb: In the heartland of India, a young Phoolan Devi becomes one of the most famous outlaws in Indian history and the target of 2,000 heavily armed men sent to kill her over a gruelling 48-hour siege.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Possible Love
movies.blurb: Lee Chang-dong’s eagerly anticipated new film brings stories of relationships, generational and class divides, in this gripping tale of two couples playing games with themselves and one another.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Pretenders
movies.blurb: Tough, stylish, and effortlessly cool, the Pretenders founder Chrissie Hynde is the real thing. Grounded in extensive interviews with Hynde and archival materials, Pretenders chronicles the evolution of one of rock’s most singular icons.

movies.title: Prima Facie
movies.blurb: Oscar nominee Cynthia Erivo (Wicked) stars in this adaptation of Suzie Miller’s globally acclaimed play that examines what happens when an ambitious barrister who primarily defends those accused of sex crimes unexpectedly becomes the accuser in a sexual assault case.

movies.title: Purgatory
movies.blurb: This coming-of-age dramedy, set in the 1980s, follows Beatrice as she tries to reunite her recently separated parents, and stars J.K. Simmons, Abby Elliott, John Reynolds, and Jack Innanen.

movies.title: Rags 2 Richmond
movies.blurb: In 2005, aspiring singer Nathan enters a controversial Asian male beauty pageant in Richmond hoping for his big break. An innocent lie catapults him into overnight fame — and suddenly, the whole city is watching!  Taken under the wing of Justice, a fiery upstart producer grasping for the next big thing, a reluctant Nathan buries the lie and enters the pageant circuit alongside a rag-tag team of fellow competitors, navigating an improbable mission of turning skeptical public opinion to their side. But when pageant executives catch wind of Nathan’s secret, his star status becomes a weapon for consolidating power.   With the finale looming and the lie unraveling, Nathan and his peers must decide - submit to the fame machine, or risk it all to stay true to themselves.

movies.title: Rainbow The Killer
movies.blurb: In a confined Toronto takeaway, a courteous immigrant chef hides a violent past that resurfaces when racism, crime, and blackmail push him to the brink. Beneath his composed appearance lies a history shaped by violence, poverty, and torment. When a racist altercation with a local turns deadly, Rainbow’s repressed anger resurfaces. As he desperately tries to cover his tracks, he must contend with nosy customers, a susceptible health inspector, and an unrelenting police officer. When venomous drug cartel enforcers raid his kitchen, Rainbow is forced into a vicious struggle for survival. His nightmare deepens when a shadowy figure threatens to expose his secret, forcing him into another deadly crime. Caught between exposure and his own violent tendencies, Rainbow must decide how much of the man he once was remains—and how far he is willing to go. As his world unravels, he becomes both villain and vigilante.

movies.title: Rapinoe
movies.blurb: Soccer star Megan Rapinoe explores what it means to win and lose in this intimate portrait by Rebeca Huntt (Beba).

movies.title: Re/Pair
movies.blurb: Lacey Schwartz Delgado (Little White Lie) explores the bonds and tensions between American Black and Jewish communities in a series of dialogues with prominent figures.

movies.title: RED SNOW
movies.blurb: In Finland, sixteen-year-old emo teen Johanna dreams of a glittering Twilight vampire prince. What she gets instead is Martti — a balding, beer-bellied 49-year-old bloodsucker who slips into a Santa suit to gain entry to homes and devour entire families.  When Johanna crosses paths with Martti on Christmas Eve, she thinks her dark fairy tale has come true. But instead of eternal romance, she finds herself trapped in a bloody and horrific nightmare of aging masculine toxicity, family trauma, and festive slaughter. By morning, the snow will turn red.

movies.title: REDEFINED | Short Film Showcase
movies.blurb: Catch the premiere of REDEFINED at the Toronto International Film Festival and streaming worldwide on the NFB. Following the screening, join us for a Q&A with the filmmakers.

movies.title: Rehearsals for a Revolution
movies.blurb: Acclaimed actor-turned-documentarian Pegah Ahangarani draws on a trove of archival material to skillfully weave her personal narrative with Iranian politics over the past four decades.

movies.title: Report to Mother
movies.blurb: North American Premiere of 4K restoration! A daring clarion call and one of the most significant works of Indian political cinema, John Abraham’s extraordinary final film Amma Ariyan (Report to Mother) follows a young man in 1970s Kerala as he journeys — with a progressive swell of companions — to inform a mother of her son’s death, amid widespread unrest.

movies.title: Rescue
movies.blurb: Director Sine Plambech (Heartbound, TIFF ’18) documents the kidnapping of a mother and her long quest to be reunited with her husband, illuminating a mass crisis experienced by migrants in the Mediterranean.

movies.title: River
movies.blurb: Joshua Giuliano makes an audacious debut with a suspenseful slasher that sets three embittered siblings adrift along a rural waterway, and in the sights of a masked killer.

movies.title: Rogue Trooper
movies.blurb: Directed by Duncan Jones (Moon, Warcraft), this outlandish animated adaptation of the influential British comic book follows a clone soldier bred for an interstellar forever-war and his fallen comrades whose personalities live on within his gun, helmet, and backpack.

movies.title: Run Terry Run
movies.blurb: This intimate and inspiring portrait from filmmaker Sean Menard (TIFF ’17’s The Carter Effect) draws upon never-before-seen footage to reveal the arduous process and profound commitment behind Terry Fox’s Marathon of Hope to raise awareness and money for cancer research.

movies.title: Salvation
movies.blurb: A hunger for purpose and a flair for delusion in a small Scottish town: Tom Nicoll’s debut is a sharp, empathetic portrait of young men adrift.

movies.title: SeriesFest Pitch-A-Thon Roadshow
movies.blurb: Presented in partnership with TIFF The Market, SeriesFest’s Pitch-A-Thon! Roadshow brings its dynamic, fast-paced live pitching competition to one of the industry’s premier marketplaces. Selected creators receive expert pitch coaching prior to the event to refine their presentations before delivering a 5-minute pitch for their original episodic projects to a panel of development executives, producers, and decision-makers. Following each pitch, creators receive valuable feedback and insights from the panel while making meaningful connections with industry leaders. The event showcases bold new voices and provides a platform for the next generation of television storytelling.

movies.title: Seventeen
movies.blurb: Three young queer Indigenous people’s lives intersect and overlap over the course of 17 hours in downtown Vancouver.

movies.title: She Dances
movies.blurb: A struggling single father tries to reconnect with his distant teenage daughter while chaperoning her at a regional dance competition in the Southeast.

movies.title: Silenced Nights
movies.blurb: For some, staying silent is the only way to survive. Lawrence Fajardo’s bleak sociopolitical drama Silenced Nights follows a witness to an extrajudicial killing in a Philippines slum as he seeks to make the truth known.

movies.title: Silent Life: The Rudolph Valentino Centennial Final Cut
movies.blurb: Silent Life is not a biopic. It is a confession — a poetic meditation on fame, mortality, and the price of a dream, told through the spirit of Rudolph Valentino. The filmmaker, who spent 20 years bringing this vision to life, does not simply perform as Valentino — he merges with him, channeling his own journey as an immigrant and a stutterer into the tragedy of the silent icon. His story is interwoven with three legendary figures: Isabella Rossellini as the mother of the Great Lover; Franco Nero (who played Valentino in 1975) voicing his spirit; and Terry Moore, the last surviving star of Hollywood's Golden Era, as the mysterious Lady in Black. What begins as a tribute to Valentino transforms into a meditation on dreams, silence, and cinematic immortality. It is the story of a man who carried a dream for 50 years, and finally found his voice in the silence of a legend.

movies.title: Sisters
movies.blurb: Outside of Madrid, two sisters unite their families on a summer weekend, celebrating milestones and the solstice-heralding San Juan Festival. However, joy quickly turns to horror when a serious allegation of sexual abuse surfaces from one of their children.

movies.title: Skintown
movies.blurb: 1994. As northern Ireland takes its first steps towards peace, best mates Vinny and Jonty are about to jump start their futures with the most reckless trip of their lives.

movies.title: Sloan Science & Technology Project Pitch 2026
movies.blurb: Returning for a fourth year, four Canadian and international creators will pitch their science- and technology-based feature film or series projects in front of a live audience and a selected panel of industry decision-makers. Watch the projects come to life off the page and receive crucial feedback from the panelists. See the stories in their earliest stages and watch the art of the pitch in the flesh.

movies.title: Sloan Science & Technology Project Pitch Happy Hour
movies.blurb: Open to all accredited delegates, the Sloan Science & Technology Project Pitch Happy Hour is an open invitation to mix, mingle and build new connections with Market colleagues.

movies.title: Slow Horses
movies.blurb: The sixth season of this smash hit series finds the motley crew of disgraced MI5 agents in Slough House, working under the cantankerous Jackson Lamb (Gary Oldman, TIFF ’17’s Darkest Hour), thrown once again into the fray.

movies.title: Smudge the Blades
movies.blurb: A fresh take on the underdog sports film, centring on an Indigenous hockey team in Northern Alberta, from actor and director Cody Lightning (Hey, Viktor!, TIFF ’23) and starring Ed Helms, Jana Schmieding, and Paulina Alexis.

movies.title: Someone's Daughter
movies.blurb: A criminal defence lawyer finds herself kidnapped and abandoned on a remote island along with a former client who she previously cleared of sexual assault charges. As they make their way through the unrelenting Canadian wilderness, doubt gives way to fear, and she finds herself facing a choice no lawyer should ever have to make.

movies.title: Soumsoum, The Night of the Stars
movies.blurb: Five years after Lingui, the Sacred Bonds, Chadian director Mahamat-Saleh Haroun returns to TIFF with his latest feature, winner of the FIPRESCI Award at the 2026 Berlinale.

movies.title: Spirit Guardians: The Last Secret of the First Emperor
movies.blurb: The largest production in Vietnamese history, this sweeping epic from Nguyễn Phan Quang Binh (The Floating Lives) transports us to the Đinh dynasty, when a band of fearless warriors set out on a secret mission to safeguard a sacred mystery.

movies.title: Spotlight: Italy Offers Everything You Need
movies.blurb:
Discover why Italy is the ideal partner for your next production. Explore outstanding filming locations, competitive tax incentives, funding schemes, and co-production opportunities that make Italy a leading destination for international projects. Connect with industry experts and producers, gain practical insights into the Italian production landscape, and unlock new opportunities to finance, develop, and bring your stories to the screen.

movies.title: Spring in a Small Town
movies.blurb:
World Premiere of 4K restoration!

Crowned the greatest Chinese film ever made by the Hong Kong Film Critics Society, director Fei Mu’s poetic, romantic 1948 masterpiece observes a bored wife enlivened by a surprise visit from an old flame, whose presence threatens to upend the matrimonial home.

movies.title: Still Night, Burning House
movies.blurb: A once-close family comes together to say goodbye to an uncle who struggled with mental health issues, in award-winning short filmmaker Carol Nguyen’s tender and emotional feature-length documentary debut.

movies.title: Straight Shot
movies.blurb: A bodyguard past his prime fights through a skyscraper full of mercenaries to save his ex-fiancée trapped in an experimental coffin.

movies.title: Strong Son
movies.blurb: A bodybuilder struggles to keep it together as he cares for his elderly father in this perceptive and deeply felt drama by Winnipeg’s Ian Bawa.

movies.title: Studio 100 Film: Current & Upcoming Features
movies.blurb: Step into the world of premium family animation with Studio 100 Film's exclusive showcase of current and upcoming feature films. Discover a vibrant slate packed with adventure, comedy, fantasy, heartwarming storytelling, and unforgettable characters. This dynamic presentation features first looks at projects in development and production, including Flamingo Flamenco, On the Edge, Zac Power, Dino Alert: The Ogglies Strike Back, Toxic: Miracle of the Jungle, The Last Dodo, Dougie Dolittle, Emmi & Unipig, and Halloween vs. Day of the Dead, alongside highlights from available titles such as Arnie & Barney, Rally: From Paris to the Pyramids, North, Miss Moxy, and Heidi – Rescue of the Lynx. From original concepts to beloved brands, this curated reel offers buyers, distributors, broadcasters, and platform partners a unique opportunity to explore the future of family entertainment from Studio 100 Film.

movies.title: Stuffed
movies.blurb: Love, death, and taxidermy collide in this gloriously twisted musical, one of the year’s funniest, most original, and unexpectedly heartfelt romances.

movies.title: Sunburn
movies.blurb: Over one hot summer day in Toronto, a group of young people try to survive the heatwave and a blackout by making jokes, roaming the city, and forming tangible connections that feel like they can disappear at any moment.

movies.title: SUPERTHINGS: THE MOVIE
movies.blurb: When everyday objects suddenly come to life as superheroes and villains, an ordinary world is transformed into the extraordinary universe of SuperThings! Inspired by the internationally acclaimed Spanish toy brand.

movies.title: Sustainable Stories, Sustainable Industry: Sustainability Practices for Film
movies.blurb:
With the increasingly visible impacts and heightened awareness of climate change, the film industry is under growing pressure to reduce its environmental impact.

This panel will explore key questions regarding sustainability in the industry: What are the most significant environmental impacts? What are the barriers to do better? Which solutions exist? What can we learn from emerging practice and standards? How can industry participants collaborate to tackle system-wide challenges?

movies.title: Tangles
movies.blurb: A young woman deals with her vibrant mother’s Alzheimer diagnosis in this deeply moving animation adapted from a graphic memoir, with a voice cast including Abbi Jacobson, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Bryan Cranston, Seth Rogen, and Bowen Yang.

movies.title: Tehran, Under the Skin
movies.blurb: In an age of body anxiety, filmmaker Afsaneh Salari embeds herself in the offices of Iranian plastic surgeons to interview their clients with humour and empathy.

movies.title: Ten Dark Women
movies.blurb: North American Premiere of 4K restoration! In the stylish, satirical, and ahead-of-its-time Ten Dark Women (Kuroi jûnin no onna, 1961), by legendary Japanese director Kon Ichikawa, 10 women discover they are sharing the same pathologically unfaithful man, and temporarily abandon jealousy to meticulously orchestrate a collective revenge.

movies.title: Tender Loving Care
movies.blurb: Seven-time Academy Award nominee Mike Leigh returns with an uplifting story of family and how to deal with grief, featuring remarkably emotional performances from Kate O’Flynn and Alice Bailey Johnson.

movies.title: Tenzing
movies.blurb: Starring Tom Hiddleston (TIFF ’24’s The Life of Chuck), Oscar nominee Willem Dafoe, and Genden Phuntsok (TIFF ’18’s Jinpa), this wondrous biopic recounts the story of Himalayan Sherpa mountaineer Tenzing Norgay who, alongside Edmund Hillary, became first to top Everest in 1953.

movies.title: The Age of Goodbyes
movies.blurb: Vivian Sung stars as the ravishing Du Li An in a breathtaking cinematic adaptation of Li Zi Shu’s The Age of Goodbyes, a story about memory, loss, love, doppelgängers, and hidden truths.

movies.title: The Ankler's Pure Nonfiction with Alex Gibney
movies.blurb: Oscar-winning filmmaker Alex Gibney is acclaimed for his investigations into some of the world’s most formidable, powerful institutions and individuals. Now he takes on his most epic and ambitious project in Musk, looking at the first trillionaire whose reach extends to electric cars, space travel, social media, AI, and more. TIFF Docs programmer Thom Powers interviews Gibney to explore all the journalistic and artistic choices behind the scenes of this project making its North American Premiere at TIFF.

movies.title: The Ankler’s Prestige Junkie with Los Javis
movies.blurb: The Ankler’s awards editor Katey Rich returns to the TIFF stage for a live taping of her Prestige Junkie podcast, welcoming the winners of the Best Director prize at Cannes, Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — the filmmaking duo known popularly as Los Javis — to discuss their remarkable new film, La Bola Negra. They’ll join Katey to discuss the journey behind their epic, decades-spanning story of love, desire, and identity, bringing together breakout talent and screen legends: Spanish pop star Guitarricadelafuente, Élite star Miguel Bernardeau, newcomers Milo Quifes and Carlos González, Emmy-nominated director, writer, and actor Julio Torres, two-time Goya winner Lola Dueñas, and screen icons Penélope Cruz and Glenn Close.

movies.title: The Assassin(s)
movies.blurb: Based on the attempted assassination of South Korean President Park Chung-hee, the latest from Hur Jin-ho (TIFF ’23’s A Normal Family) is a large-canvas procedural about police and journalists determined to uncover a seemingly impenetrable conspiracy.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: The Beloved
movies.blurb: Starring Oscar winner Javier Bardem and Victoria Luengo (TIFF ’24’s The Room Next Door), the latest from Rodrigo Sorogoyen (TIFF ’18’s The Realm) chronicles an unnerving collaboration between a charismatic, manipulative director and the actor daughter he hasn’t seen in 13 years.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: The Betrayers
movies.blurb: In adapting his own literary prize-winner, Toronto’s David Bezmozgis delivers a deft political thriller about the limits of love and loyalty.

movies.title: The Black Box is Orange
movies.blurb: The debut feature by Toronto artist and filmmaker Yuula Benivolski, The Black Box is Orange is a multimodal, autobiographical essay film that deploys both personal memory and incomplete archives to reflect on a childhood in a militarized border town.

movies.title: The bovine with the curved horns
movies.blurb: Blending Caribbean fantasy, magical realism, and Colombia’s painful history, The bovine with the curved horns follows a boy searching for his missing father through a landscape where myth and violence coexist. A haunting, poetic debut of remarkable beauty and emotional power.

movies.title: The City of the Living
movies.blurb: The City of the Living is Edoardo Gabbriellini’s (Holiday, TIFF ’23) gripping yet respectful anti-true crime film based on Nicola Lagioia’s bestselling literary chronicle about the senseless 2016 murder of a young man that rocked Rome.

movies.title: THE COLOR OF THE SUN
movies.blurb: During the summer break before their final year of high school on the main island of Okinawa, Kamei and his friends find themselves contemplating their future. However, their lives take an unexpected turn when they encounter Colin, a young teenager raised on the American base of Naha. Their friendship is tested when a U.S. serviceman is accused of rape in the local community. The clash and the uncanny resemblance between Kamei and Colin becomes the story’s beating heart: a raw coming-of-age that asks what it means to belong.

movies.title: The Daughters of Abraham
movies.blurb: A young Muslim woman raised in Marseille reunites with a young Jewish woman after a period of estrangement, reconnecting as friends over summer break. When a sudden tragedy disrupts their carefree holiday, the pair face the similarities and differences that strengthen and threaten their relationship together.

movies.title: The Debut
movies.blurb: Jesse Eisenberg directs Academy Award winner Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti in a dark comedy about a bored suburban housewife who finds purpose acting in community theatre.

movies.title: The Diary of a Chambermaid
movies.blurb: Offering his most provocative work yet, the latest from Romanian provocateur Radu Jude is a surprisingly tender socioeconomic satire.

movies.title: The Difficult Bride
movies.blurb: Following the strange visions afflicting a woman on the cusp of marriage, the latest from Rubaiyat Hossain (TIFF ’19’s Made in Bangladesh) examines the pressures applied to brides in a milieu where weddings demand an asphyxiating feminine ideal.

movies.title: The Dreamed Adventure
movies.blurb: Winner of the Jury Prize in the competition section of the Cannes Film Festival, The Dreamed Adventure is German auteur Valeska Grisebach's highly anticipated and exceptional follow up to Western (TIFF ’17).

movies.title: The Elder Hunters
movies.blurb: A group of young men in New York City who get their thrills attacking and robbing the elderly ending up finding themselves in a world of trouble when they attack the wrong man.

movies.title: The Face of Horror
movies.blurb: The Love Witch’s Anna Biller stunningly adapts the famous Japanese ghost story Yotsuya Kaidan for 14th-century England in this gory tribute to classic Technicolor shockers.

movies.title: The Final Act
movies.blurb: Quebec’s Sophie Deraspe returns to the Festival with a philosophical and intimate look at the many profound issues surrounding both death and medically assisted dying in an extraordinary documentary.

movies.title: The First Dinosaur
movies.blurb: In the wake of Earth’s greatest extinction event, a new creature rises that will change the planet forever: the first dinosaur. When young dinosaur expert Dex discovers a mysterious baby that may hold the key to this ancient mystery, he sets off on an epic road trip adventure with his older sister Dana and his fearless best friend Kayla. Together, they journey across spectacular landmarks, uncovering clues that could rewrite the origins of dinosaurs. As Dex races to solve the mystery of what makes a dinosaur a dinosaur, he discovers that the strongest force connecting the past and present is family. Funny, thrilling, and filled with wonder, The First Dinosaur is a cinematic family adventure millions of years in the making.

movies.title: The Fortunate Isles
movies.blurb: In the 16th century, on the newly conquered Canary Islands, colonial misgivings intersect with personal desperation. Fátima, an enslaved and pregnant woman, must struggle to survive both the landscape, and the other inhabitants.

movies.title: THE GIRL WITH THE LEICA
movies.blurb: Paris, July 14, 1937. Gerda Taro spends her final day before returning to the Spanish front with Robert Capa and the close friends with whom she escaped Nazi Germany. As past and present intertwine, the defining moments of her life resurface: her political activism in Leipzig alongside her first love, her years of exile in Paris, her whirlwind romance with Capa, her discovery of photography, and her growing determination to use her Leica as a tool for resistance and freedom. A portrait of the first female photojournalist to die on the battlefield, Gerda Taro embodied an era when everything still seemed possible.

movies.title: The Golden Age
movies.blurb: Born at the turn of the century in a village's butcher shop, Jeanne Lavaur dreams of becoming a countess. Inspired by the fearless Céleste and guided by her love for Guillaume de Barante, Jeanne’s journey carries her from the vibrant Paris of the Golden Twenties through the turmoil of two world wars. As her life intertwines with the great upheavals of the 20th century, she rises as a fiercely free woman, determined to never let anyone else define who she is meant to be.

movies.title: THE HELPERS
movies.blurb: Embedding directly within five active warzones, this urgent hybrid documentary blends raw frontline footage with stunning 2D animation to follow the humanitarian heroes risking everything for strangers. Transforming the testimonies of 100 refugees and aid workers into a global call to action, the film operates as a 100% non-profit rescue mission engineered to secure vital aid for half a million people a year before time runs out.

movies.title: The Housewife
movies.blurb: Grounded in artful performances from Oscar nominee Naomi Watts (TIFF ’01’s Mulholland Drive) and Tye Sheridan (TIFF ’13’s Joe), this salient historical drama depicts the complexities of seeking justice in the long shadow of Nazism.

movies.title: The Hummingbird Paints Fragrant Songs
movies.blurb: The Indigenous painter Sara Flores gets discovered by the international art world in her 70s, setting her off on an adventure as she travels from her home in the Peruvian Amazon to be fȇted in galleries from New York to Paris.

movies.title: The Idiot(s)
movies.blurb: Aimee Lou Wood and Johnny Flynn bring to life the story of Anna and Fyodor Dostoevsky, showcasing the troubled author and the woman who pushed him to write one of his greatest works.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: The Julia Set
movies.blurb: Chase Infiniti stars as a gifted university student who becomes romantically involved with a teaching assistant as they both prepare for the Putnam Exam, the most challenging math competition in North America. Gillian Anderson and Jason Isaacs co-star.

movies.title: The Liberation
movies.blurb: Carrie Coon soars in the riveting story inspired by filmmaker Guy Nattiv’s grandmother, whose humdrum day-to-day life is upended by a mysterious and entrancing young woman (Lily James) offering the promise of escape to something better.

movies.title: The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd
movies.blurb: Starring Oscar nominee Amanda Seyfried (The Testament of Ann Lee, TIFF ’25) and Scoot McNairy (Nightbitch, TIFF ’24), the latest from Tim Blake Nelson is a psychologically rich prison story about crime, punishment, and love.

movies.title: The Lost Children Of Tuam
movies.blurb: A quietly powerful true story of an amateur historian’s quest to uncover a long-buried injustice. By exposing what rightly became a national scandal, Catherine Corless changed Ireland forever.

movies.title: The Lychee Road
movies.blurb: The film is adapted from the novel of the same name by Ma Boyong. Set during the Tang Dynasty's Tianbao era, it follows Li Shande (played by Da Peng), a middle-aged man who grumbles his way through countless tasks and pinches every penny, only to remain an insignificant low-ranking official. However, things seem to take a turn when he's suddenly summoned—someone has arranged for him to take on the lucrative role of “Litchi Envoy.” If he succeeds, glory and wealth await, a chance to turn his life around. But if he fails...

movies.title: The Man I Love
movies.blurb: Ira Sachs’ vision of New York artists living under the spectre of AIDS in the ’80s focuses on the joy and salvation of creativity.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: THE NEST
movies.blurb: Marta – a cruel and damaged woman – is obsessed with protecting her family from the horrors of the outside world, so she keeps her mother and young son locked away. Their isolation ends with the arrival of Velasco, a man driven by revenge and prepared to destroy her world.

movies.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
movies.blurb: Anchored by John Turturro’s charismatic performance, this low-key crime drama from Noah Segan (Blood Relatives) harkens back to the character-driven films of 1970s New Hollywood.

movies.title: The Pervert's Guide to Utopias
movies.blurb: Twenty years after The Pervert’s Guide to Cinema, the renowned intellectual Slavoj Žižek reunites with director Sophie Fiennes for a fresh meditation on movies and ideas that crackles with energy.

movies.title: The Remotes
movies.blurb: This ambitious, beguiling narrative debut from acclaimed Filipino filmmaker and experimentalist John Torres follows a grieving detective who finds himself increasingly ensnared while investigating a case involving a sinister navigation app causing physical and psychological debris.

movies.title: The Road Not Taken
movies.blurb: Peter Ho-Sun Chan directs Zhou Xun, Wen Qi, Tian Zhuangzhuang and Wang Xiao in a drama about early-onset Alzheimer disease. Combining expert storytelling with commercial appeal, The Road Not Taken reflects on what remains when our understanding of the world begins to disappear.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: The Secret Lives of Baba Segi's Wives
movies.blurb: A wealthy patriarch’s fragile household unravels when the youngest of his four wives fails to conceive. Blending sharp Nollywood wit with tenderness, this deeply satisfying drama explores topics of infertility, gendered inheritance, and shifting family power.

movies.title: The Smell of Apples
movies.blurb: In John Trengove’s relentless third feature, a sheltered 11-year-old white South African boy gradually comes to realize the horrors of the apartheid system.

movies.title: THE SOUND OF SOMETHING NEW
movies.blurb: Six lives intersect in the chaos of everyday life in Milan, each searching for their own “perfect noise,” a signal to follow rather than surrender to emotional numbness. Ralph and Viola struggle to balance family, financial compromises, and their son Mirko’s bullying at school. Andrea, a photographer who dreams of becoming a father, is married to Andreina, a nurse terrified of motherhood. Meanwhile Alba, a strong yet fragile woman, is trapped in a violent marriage with Umberto, an entertainer in pediatric wards. Their paths cross through humiliations, small acts of kindness, and buried desires, until a chance encounter between Viola and Andrea sparks the possibility of a second chance, setting off a chain of events that unsettles all their lives. Because even in the most ordinary lives, it takes very little for masks to fall away or for people to find the courage to truly live.

movies.title: The Spiral
movies.blurb: Director Paolo Strippoli turns the screws on a desperate mother (Jasmine Trinca) as she confesses a series of Faustian bargains to her estranged daughter (Romana Maggiora Vergano) in this riveting morality chiller.

movies.title: The Stunt Driver
movies.blurb: Jay Baruchel and director Michael Dowse re-team for a raucous yet heartfelt comedy about a Canadian stuntman who dared to dream big and fly (very) high.

movies.title: The Surgeon
movies.blurb: Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh (Everything Everywhere All at Once) is back in action as a kidnapped surgeon forced to perform one last operation in this fun, pulse-pounding thriller.

movies.title: The Town with Matt Belloni and Matthew Greenfield
movies.blurb:
In this special live session of The Town recorded at TIFF: The Market, Matthew Belloni sits down with Matthew Greenfield, President of Searchlight Pictures, to unpack how prestige cinema survives in today’s theatrical landscape. Together, they pull back the curtain on how Searchlight maintains its distinct arthouse identity under the broader Disney, the uphill battle for mid-budget adult dramas, and what it actually takes to engineer an Oscar campaign in today's fragmented media environment.

Matthew Belloni’s The Town is the place to go for industry truths, big picture reporting, and hard-hitting conversations with sources unlikely to interview anywhere else, with anyone else.

movies.title: The Ultimate Planet
movies.blurb: After surviving a clinical death, Dan Cruncher "Crunch " is flooded with memories he never lived: of his service in an alien landing party, of fierce battles, loyal friends, and a beloved girlfriend. Determined to untangle reality from illusion, Crunch finds himself locked in a high-stakes struggle against formidable foes—both on Earth and a distant alien planet. The ultimate prize of this epic confrontation is a panacea capable of saving those he holds dear and transforming the fate of humanity itself.  Amidst the relentless threat of deadly extraterrestrial creatures, every moment at the Ultimate Planet pulses with danger and suspense, ratcheting up the tension. But at its heart, this is also a tale of profound sacrifice and a love that transcends all boundaries, shining brightly even in the darkest corners of the universe.

movies.title: The Ultra Runner
movies.blurb: Punishing tests of human endurance become a means of escaping past demons for the unforgettable subject of Mila Aung-Thwin’s superb new film.

movies.title: The Unknown
movies.blurb: A highlight of this year’s Cannes Competition, the third feature by acclaimed French filmmaker, actor, and screenwriter Arthur Harari (co-writer of Anatomy of a Fall) is a moody, existential body-swap puzzler starring an extraordinary Léa Seydoux and a near-unrecognizable Niels Schneider.

movies.title: The Violinist
movies.blurb: Winner of this year’s Annecy Cristal award, this intimate animation about two violinists in Singapore circa WWII highlights the healing power of music while pulling heartstrings.

movies.title: The World Before
movies.blurb: Yoon Dan-bi’s coming-of-age story follows two childhood best friends who reunite for a summer on a remote Korean island. This beautifully constructed slice of life captures the emotional intensity of adolescence through assured filmmaking and compelling performances.

movies.title: Thirteen in Gaza
movies.blurb: Palestinian director Hosam Abu Dan makes his narrative feature debut with a nuanced and deeply human portrait of a father and his teenage daughter navigating everyday life in a refugee camp in the Gaza Strip.

movies.title: Toy Gun Bandit
movies.blurb: A prank gone wrong launches a Quebec teen into a life of crime in Rémi St-Michel’s energetic and unpredictable second feature.

movies.title: Tracing Footprints
movies.blurb: In the premiere episode, hip-hop legend Fab 5 Freddy embarks on a journey to uncover his Barbadian ancestry. Through archival research and on-the-ground discovery, he learns how his family’s story connects to the island’s complex history.  Along the way, Fab explores Barbados’ vibrant cultural traditions, from music to art, that echo in hip-hop’s foundation. What emerges is a powerful homecoming that reframes his legacy and highlights the island’s global influence.

movies.title: Trash Mountain
movies.blurb: After the death of their hoarder father in rural Missouri, two siblings (Caleb Hearon and Zooey Deschanel) reunite to sort through the baggage — both literal and emotional — in Kris Rey’s poignant and funny exploration of love and grief.

movies.title: Trees are Watching
movies.blurb: Iranian Kurdish auteur Bahman Ghobadi blends psychological horror and ecological allegory as he depicts the eerie haunting of a writer (Eva Green) reckoning with past misdeeds under the ominous gaze of a pair of trees and a malignant wooden chair.

movies.title: Trick
movies.blurb: Successful illustrator Daniele Mallarico travels to Naples to look after his four-year-old grandson while his daughter is away for a fewdays. What begins as a simple babysitting job turns into a subtle psychological duel, as the child’s boundless imagination slowly unsettles him. Trapped together in the apartment, Daniele is forced to confront something far more disturbing than a mischievous child: the fear of aging and the loss of creativity. Through this strange encounter, he may rediscover the power of imagination he thought he had lost.

movies.title: Turtle Island Rap
movies.blurb: The bumpy road to success experienced by three aspiring Indigenous hip-hop artists is the focus of Alexandra Lazarowich’s (Fast Horse) verité-style feature documentary debut.

movies.title: Tyler Perry Studios presents Maxscene: A New Home for Filmmakers
movies.blurb: A new door is opening for filmmakers with distinctive voices. Join us for an intimate conversation with Antoinetta Stallings, Head of Development & Acquisitions and Robyne Gordon, Head of Business Affairs, on Maxscene, Tyler Perry Studios' new specialty film division.

movies.title: Union Town
movies.blurb: Barbara Kopple (TIFF ’76’s Harlan County, U.S.A.) looks at three crucial labour battles as they unfold in New York City involving workers from UPS, Amazon, and deliveristas for DoorDash and GrubHub.

movies.title: Up Against It
movies.blurb: Post-marital acrimony and parental devotion make strange bedfellows in Trudie Styler’s wicked comedy, starring Oscar nominee Antonio Banderas (TIFF ’19’s Pain and Glory) and Eva Birthistle (TIFF ’05’s Imagine Me & You) as co-parenting divorcees faced with an indecent proposal.

movies.title: Villeneuve: The Rise of a Legend
movies.blurb: Chronicling the exhilarating career of Gilles Villeneuve, one of Canada’s foremost athletes, this biopic from director Yan Lanouette Turgeon stars Rémi Goulet as the kid from Quebec who changed Formula One.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Vintage Violence
movies.blurb: In Eugene Kotlyarenko’s mixed-media caper, a livestreamer (Cole Sprouse) discovers a cache of vintage denim only to run afoul of the Yakuza when he is lured to Japan to sell the jeans by one of his subscribers (Kiko Mizuhara).

movies.title: VISIONARIES Danny Boyle
movies.blurb: Marked by bold visual storytelling, Academy-Award winner Danny Boyle is one of cinema's most adaptable directors. From groundbreaking films to massive live spectacles like the 2012 London Olympics, his fearless vision has defined a generation of filmmaking. Following in the footsteps of his Oscar-winning Slumdog Millionaire — which won TIFF's People's Choice Award in 2008 — Boyle joins us to reflect on his iconic career and discuss his highly anticipated new feature, Ink. Danny Boyle is a British filmmaker, producer, and writer from Radcliffe, Manchester. His directing credits include Trainspotting (96), 28 Days Later (02), and TIFF People’s Choice Award winner Slumdog Millionaire (08), for which he won the Academy Award for Best Director. His other films include 127 Hours (10), Steve Jobs (15), and 28 Years Later (25). INK (26) is his latest film.

movies.title: VISIONARIES Lee Chang-dong
movies.blurb: Korean auteur Lee Chang-dong earned international acclaim as one of cinema’s most vital and empathetic voices for his compassionate portrayals of isolated characters. With a poignant body of work, including Peppermint Candy, Secret Sunshine, and Burning, his films offer complex, poetic expressions of rage, despair, and ordinariness. At TIFF for the North American Premiere of Possible Love, Chang-dong dives into his singular approach to filmmaking for a special onstage conversation.

movies.title: VISIONARIES Robbie Brenner
movies.blurb: As President of Mattel Studios and Chief Content Officer, two-time Oscar nominee Robbie Brenner produced Greta Gerwig’s Barbie (2023), the $1.4 billion global phenomenon that scored a Best Picture nomination. At TIFF with the premiere of her new film, The Housewife, Brenner reflects on a career bridging acclaimed indie cinema, like Dallas Buyers Club (2013), with major studio blockbusters, cementing her role as one of Hollywood's leading creative visionaries.

movies.title: VISIONARIES Seth Rogen
movies.blurb: Award-winning Canadian actor, producer, writer, and potter Seth Rogen is the epitome of an entertainment polymath with a career both in front of and behind the screen as well as across series and film. This year, Rogen stars in two films at TIFF – Babies, directed by Lauren Miller Rogen, and Tangles, an animated film which Rogen and Miller Rogen produced. The prolific Rogen delves into these two films as well as his numerous other projects, including The Studio’s upcoming season two.

movies.title: VISIONARIES Sir Gary Oldman
movies.blurb: From Sid Vicious to Winston Churchill to Sirius Black, Sir Gary Oldman has long been cinema’s ultimate chameleon, fully embodying each character. And in Slow Horses, he delivers one of the most compelling performances as the brilliant and hopelessly cynical Jackson Lamb. With the premiere of Slow Horses’ sixth season at TIFF, Academy Award winner Oldman joins us for an intimate conversation on the process of transforming Mick Herron’s celebrated novel into a subversive onscreen spy thriller and crafting the unorthodox signature anti-hero.

movies.title: Viva Carmen
movies.blurb: A vibrant reframing of Bizet’s famous opera through the lens of a pack of Sevillian street children who are determined to subvert Carmen’s tragic fate. With an intimate approach to music and bold brushstrokes that dance, this animated feature sings brightly.

movies.title: Voices
movies.blurb: A starry-eyed bellhop (Francis Edemobi) enlists his friends to help him exploit an unsavoury opportunity that could secure them fame and fortune in Deantè Gray’s soulful, suspenseful 1960s-set musical chamber thriller.

movies.title: Wacko
movies.blurb: When lust, jealousy, and envy take control over one man's ambitions and tears apart a family, it's up to the only one left to repay the personal vendetta.

movies.title: Wavelengths 1: House and Home
movies.blurb: Bringing together new work by John Smith, Rita Ferrando, Jiaqi Yu, Danaya Chulphuthiphong, Mustafa Uzuner, and Natalia Marín, the films in this programme reflect on the nature of abodes, both fixed and temporary, and the limit of refuge.

movies.title: Wavelengths 2: This Suffocating Now
movies.blurb: Featuring new films by Maryam Tafakory, Zheng Lu Xinyuan, Simon Liu, and Vika Kirchenbauer, alongside a rediscovered and restored short by Takehisa Kosugi, the films in this programme speak to the political potential of creative work, creative scenes, and companionship.

movies.title: Wavelengths 3: Time and Tide
movies.blurb: Featuring new work by James Richards and Ben Russell, a rare 70mm projection by Johann Lurf, and a tribute to the recently departed Yervant Gianikian, the films of Time and Tide bend eras, epochs, and the cosmos with both verve and grace.

movies.title: Wavelengths: Anoushahpour/Aljafari
movies.blurb: Bringing together new works by Parastoo Anoushahpour and Kamal Aljafari, the two films in this programme reflect on the meeting point between imagination and memory — both personal and collective — from the perspective of children and the aged.

movies.title: We Are All Strangers
movies.blurb: Anthony Chen, a Festival favourite and the helmer behind Ilo Ilo, reunites with muses Yeo Yann Yann and Koh Jia Ler in an emotionally charged drama about a constructed family to close his “Growing Up” trilogy.

movies.title: We Are Born Good
movies.blurb: Golden Horse winner Suet Ying Chung and Wai Lun Yeung lead Leung Chuen Yeung’s assured debut, in which a struggling actress and an ex-con restaurant owner turn a petty dispute into an unlikely bond. Witty, moving, and accessible.

movies.title: What Lies Between Us
movies.blurb: From Danish director Amalie Næsby Fick and a cast led by Sidse Babett Knudsen comes a compelling cautionary tale about the ethical and moral boundaries a parent may cross in order to protect a child.

movies.title: What's Next?: Trends from an Increasingly Immersive World
movies.blurb: As interest in immersive experiences grows, new patterns are emerging in what creators are making and what audiences are seeking. Drawing from firsthand encounters with immersive experiences around the world, Katrina Lat explores the trends shaping how immersive work is being created, experienced, and discussed. With support from The City of Toronto and Ontario Creates.

movies.title: Whatcha Want
movies.blurb: The latest comedy from writer-director Mina Shum (Double Happiness, TIFF ’17’s Meditation Park) tells the story of a young woman from Hong Kong whose marriage to an affluent businessman is beginning to resemble a gilded cage.

movies.title: When Ambition Outgrows the Workflow: Making the Leap to Bigger Stories
movies.blurb:
Historically, breaking into film and television often meant following a relatively established route through film schools, production companies, studios, or traditional industry networks. Access to professional tools, workflows, and distribution channels was limited, creating significant barriers for emerging creators.

Today, those barriers are rapidly evolving. Filmmakers are building audiences online, collaborating across global communities, and leveraging increasingly accessible technology—including new AI-powered tools—to visualize, experiment, iterate, and bring ambitious ideas to life.
  
The next generation of filmmakers isn’t waiting for permission. They’re experimenting, building audiences, refining their craft, and creating work on their own terms. 

But as those ideas become bigger productions, an important question emerges: what tools, technologies, and workflows will help them make the transition from independent creator to professional filmmaker? What role can AI and other emerging technologies play?

This conversation brings together filmmakers and industry leaders to explore how the path into filmmaking is changing, what happens when creative ambition begins to outgrow the workflow, and what it takes to turn breakthrough ideas into larger, more complex productions.

movies.title: Where the River Begins
movies.blurb: In Juan Andrés Arango’s bracing and poetic third feature, an Emberá woman displaced by violence undertakes a dangerous journey to find a better life for herself and her daughter.

movies.title: Wild Horse Nine
movies.blurb: Two CIA agents (John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell) are sent on a mission to Easter Island, where one faces an existential crisis over his past actions, in Martin McDonagh’s latest dark comedy.

movies.title: Wild Wild East
movies.blurb: Set in occupied Poland in the middle of the Second World War, Jan Holoubek’s tour-de-force is part suspenseful western, part gritty wartime noir.

movies.title: Wildwood: Inside the Performance
movies.blurb: Be among the first to journey into WILDWOOD, LAIKA’s epic new fantasy adventure and its most ambitious film to date. Featuring an exclusive sneak peek at never-before-seen footage, Inside the Performance brings together voice actor Jacob Tremblay with LAIKA animators Brad Schiff, Rachelle Lambden, and Tom Carey for a behind-the-scenes look at how WILDWOOD’s handcrafted characters come to life. Moderated by Simon Thompson, the conversation explores how actors create emotionally authentic performances, how animators interpret those performances frame by frame, and how the collaboration between the two brings handcrafted characters to life. From the studio behind five Academy Award®-nominated animated features, WILDWOOD arrives in theaters October 23.

movies.title: YAGA

movies.title: Zjili: A Story of Sisterhood and The Burdens of Excess
movies.blurb: In their poignant debut feature, co-directors Christine Boateng and Hajara Musah Chambas depict the journey of three Ghanaian women eking out a living as kayayei or porters in the trenches of the world’s largest secondhand clothing market.

movies.title: Zombucha!
movies.blurb: Maddie and Leo are an aspirational millennial couple who desperately want to start a family but barely see each other. On the same disastrous day, Leo quits his ritzy ad agency and Maddie accidentally poisons actor Gabe McClaren on the set of a zombie movie, leaving them both unemployed.  At the farmers market they encounter Kai, a smouldering kombucha artisan raking in the cash. Hoping to revive both their relationship and their finances, they steal his prized SCOBY and launch Thirsty Virgin Kombucha, boosted by some “borrowed” herbs from a mysterious neighbour’s garden.  The drink becomes an overnight success until the culture develops a squirming life of its own. When Gabe’s body turns up in their garage, Maddie and Leo realise they have unleashed something deadly.
